MEM-220 — NATIVE ACCESS VIOLATION ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED
CCXT SYNC SERIALIZATION VIA PER-CONNECTOR SINGLE-WORKER EXECUTOR
================================================================================

The native crash that resisted seven speculative fixes across two
sessions has been isolated and fixed. This entry documents the
complete evidence chain.

EVIDENCE CHAIN:

  The operator's 3.15.3 run of the self-supervising exe produced
  ~/.acervator_logs/faulthandler_20260422_002401.log, captured by
  MEM-217's faulthandler. At the moment of the Windows access
  violation, three worker threads were recorded:

    Thread asyncio_0: ccxt/coinbase.py fetch_ohlcv
    Thread asyncio_1: urllib3/util/ssl_.py ssl_wrap_socket
                      (inside fetch_tickers)
    Thread asyncio_2: ccxt/base/exchange.py throttle
                      (inside fetch_ticker)

  Three separate ThreadPoolExecutor workers, three different CCXT
  fetch methods, ONE shared sync CCXT instance. CCXT's sync methods
  are documented as not thread-safe. urllib3's connection pool is
  not fully thread-safe during concurrent SSL handshakes. The
  native crash address 0x00007FFBFEE51989 (from the Windows error
  dialog) corresponds to a system DLL — exactly where you'd expect
  memory corruption from concurrent misuse.

CALL-GRAPH AUDIT:

  Before writing the fix, I traced every concurrent CCXT call site
  to ensure the fix would be comprehensive:

    QTimer _refresh_dashboard (every 2000ms)
      |- _schedule_async(charts_tab.fetch_chart_data(connectors))
      |     -> exchange.get_ohlcv() -> asyncio.to_thread(self._ex.fetch_ohlcv)
      |
      |- _schedule_async(market_map.fetch_market_data(connector))
            -> asyncio.to_thread(exchange._ex.fetch_tickers)
                                 *** BYPASSED CONNECTOR API ***

    bot.tick() asyncio task
      |- exchange.get_ticker()   -> asyncio.to_thread(self._ex.fetch_ticker)
      |- exchange.get_ohlcv()    -> asyncio.to_thread(self._ex.fetch_ohlcv)
      |- exchange.get_balance()  -> asyncio.to_thread(self._ex.fetch_balance)

  Five potential concurrent callers on Python's default thread
  pool. The faulthandler captured 3 of them firing simultaneously.
  Any combination would reproduce the race.

  Critical finding: market_map.py line 554 bypassed the
  CCXTConnector API entirely by reaching into exchange._ex. A fix
  that only touched CCXTConnector methods would have left this
  route broken and the crash would have recurred.

OPERATOR DECISION:

  Offered three options. Operator chose C — the defensive fix with
  queue-depth cap and cancellation handling. Rationale documented
  before implementation:

    Queue cap (8): catches runaway queue growth fast. With ~5
      calls per 2-second cycle under normal load, a cap of 8
      tolerates one slow cycle but fails fast under two.

    Outer timeout (25s): must be ABOVE CCXT's 20s default so
      CCXT can cancel its own request first. Our timeout is the
      backstop for pathological C-code stalls.

    Cancellation: awaiter cancels cleanly. Worker thread
      continues running its HTTP request to completion; we do
      not try to stop it (abandoning mid-flight would leave
      connection state inconsistent). Worker result is discarded.

FIX (6 CHANGES):

  1. CCXTConnector.__init__ creates single-worker executor,
     zero queue depth, a lock for teardown synchronization.

  2. New method _call_sync(fn, *args, **kwargs):
     - Queue-depth cap: raise CCXTQueueFullError if >= 8
     - Submit to executor under lock
     - Await with asyncio.wait_for(timeout=25s)
     - try/finally decrements depth on any outcome

  3. All 10 asyncio.to_thread(self._ex.X, ...) calls in
     ccxt_connector.py replaced with self._call_sync(self._ex.X, ...)

  4. New API method get_all_tickers() for bulk ticker fetch.
     market_map.py updated to call this instead of reaching into
     exchange._ex directly.

  5. disconnect() shuts down the executor under lock, wait=True.
     Idempotent — safe to call twice.

  6. tests/test_mem220_ccxt_serialization.py — 18 tests including
     AST regression guard that scans all src/ files for any
     external asyncio.to_thread(<anything>._ex.X) pattern.

REGRESSION:

  18 new tests, all 20 existing suites green. 273/273 total.

  The single most important test is the AST boundary guard: if
  any future code adds a direct _ex access outside the connector,
  it fails at CI time with a clear error naming the file and line.
  This prevents the class of bug from ever returning via drift.

WHAT THE OPERATOR GETS:

  On next launch, the tick + dashboard + market_map load pattern
  that has been crashing the app since Session 22 will serialize
  cleanly. No visible change. No performance regression (CCXT's
  own throttle was already the bottleneck, not the executor).
  The app just stops dying.

  If network degrades or an exchange rate-limits hard, the queue
  cap may fire and individual calls will fail with
  CCXTQueueFullError. The bot skips that tick, logs the error via
  MEM-216's hooks, retries next tick. Correct failure mode.

THE SESSION 24 ARC (FULL PICTURE):

  MEM-216: instrument - Python hooks catch trade-historian
           AttributeError (first concrete evidence ever)
  MEM-217: instrument - faulthandler catches native crashes,
           external watchdog captures post-mortems

  MEM-219: deploy - self-supervising exe, operator gets

  MEM-220: FIX - the actual native access violation, armed

  R68 (First Principles Come First) held from cascade one.
  The operator's rule produced the operator's solution.

MEM-221 — THE ACTUAL NATIVE CRASH FIX
THREAD-SAFE QT LOG HANDLER VIA SIGNAL/SLOT DISPATCH
ACCOUNTABILITY ENTRY FOR MEM-220 MISREAD
================================================================================

ACCOUNTABILITY:

  I shipped MEM-220 (CCXT sync serialization) confidently. Operator
  pushed back: "stop sending the same fucking god damn garbage."
  Operator was right. MEM-220 was a real and defensible change but
  it was NOT the crash fix, and I presented it as one.

  What I did wrong: I read the faulthandler log, saw three worker
  threads, noticed they were all inside CCXT code, and pattern-
  matched to "concurrent CCXT bug" because that matched a known
  documented class of bug. I did not read every thread's TOP frame
  carefully. Thread asyncio_0's top frame was
  src\gui\main_window.py:1635 in emit — OUR CODE, in a widget call,
  from a worker thread. That was the actual smoking gun. The two
  other threads (asyncio_1 in ssl_wrap_socket inside fetch_tickers,
  asyncio_2 in throttle inside fetch_ticker) were ordinary in-flight
  CCXT work that happened to be captured in the dump. They were
  correlated with the crash, not causing it.

  This was a confirmation-bias failure. I had a theory, found three
  data points consistent with it, and stopped looking. R68 says
  "let the system tell you what's wrong." I let my familiar pattern
  tell me what was wrong, then cherry-picked evidence that matched.
  R68 violation.

ROOT CAUSE (reconstructed carefully this time):

  _QtLogHandler is installed on Python's root logger at DEBUG level
  (main_window.py:1650-1652). Every library that calls logger.xxx()
  — CCXT, urllib3, requests, asyncio, all of them — ends up
  dispatching to this handler's emit() method.

  When CCXT runs inside an asyncio.to_thread(...) call, CCXT is
  executing on a ThreadPoolExecutor worker thread. CCXT calls
  self.logger.debug(...) at many points during fetch(). Python's
  logging framework takes the LogRecord and dispatches it to each
  registered handler, running the handler's emit() on the calling
  thread.

  _QtLogHandler.emit() then directly did:

      cursor = self._te.textCursor()
      cursor.movePosition(...)
      cursor.insertText(msg, fmt)
      sb = self._te.verticalScrollBar()
      sb.setValue(sb.maximum())

  All from the worker thread. Qt widgets are not thread-safe. On
  Windows, cross-thread widget access produces a native access
  violation. This is a Qt fundamental, not a bug in any library
  — Qt docs state explicitly that all widget manipulation must
  happen on the GUI thread.

  The same bug existed verbatim in _StockLogHandler in
  stock_main_window.py.

FIX:

  Both handlers now multiple-inherit from (QObject, logging.Handler).
  Each has an _append_signal. emit() only calls
  self._append_signal.emit(msg, r, g, b) and returns. A separate
  @Slot method, _append_to_widget, receives the signal and does
  the actual widget work.

  The signal is connected with Qt.AutoConnection (default). Qt's
  AutoConnection semantics:
    - if emitter and receiver are on the same thread → DirectConnection
      (slot runs synchronously)
    - if they're on different threads → QueuedConnection
      (slot invocation is posted to the receiver's event loop)

  Since the handler is constructed on the main thread, the slot
  always runs on the main thread regardless of which thread called
  logger.xxx(). Widget access is safe.

  QColor is passed as three ints (r, g, b) so no QColor instance
  crosses thread boundaries. The receiving slot reconstructs the
  QColor on the main thread.

NEW AST REGRESSION GUARD:

  test_no_handler_subclass_touches_widget_in_emit walks every .py
  file in src/, finds every class that subclasses logging.Handler,
  and asserts that the class's emit() method does NOT call any of
  the known Qt widget operations (insertText, setValue, append,
  document, textCursor, verticalScrollBar, movePosition). If any
  future handler shortcuts the signal dispatch and touches the
  widget directly, the test fails at CI time with the file name
  and line number.

RELATIONSHIP TO MEM-220:

  MEM-220 (CCXT single-worker executor + queue cap) stays in place.
  CCXT IS documented as not thread-safe. Single-worker serialization
  is defensible hygiene. The queue cap is useful fail-fast
  backpressure under degraded network. But MEM-220 was never going
  to fix the Qt cross-thread widget access — even a single worker
  still calls logger.debug() from a non-main thread.

  Correct characterization: MEM-220 is hygiene; MEM-221 is the fix.

MEM-215 REVERT INVARIANT:

  MEM-215 reverted the MEM-213/214 QThread-based Start-button
  refactor. Its invariant was "no QThread, QObject, or Signal
  imports in main_window." MEM-221 now legitimately imports
  QObject + Signal for the log-handler purpose. This is NOT a
  reintroduction of the reverted pattern — no QThread, no
  worker QObject on a separate thread, no api_logger signal
  shim, no cross-thread Start handler. Test updated to reflect
  the narrower invariant (no QThread; QObject/Signal permitted
  for MEM-221).

MEM-222 — HISTORY TAB WIRING IN NORMAL BOT-START FLOW
PARALLEL WORK WHILE 3.15.5 RUNS STABLY
================================================================================

OPERATOR REPORT:

  "History appears to be a dead tab. Still running. Not stopping.
   Time for parallel work."

  Attached screenshot: History tab showing "No data — connect to
  an exchange" with a bot actively running on 3.15.5. MEM-221
  native crash fix confirmed stable; operator moved on to
  feature-completeness work while app remains live.

DIAGNOSIS:

  Grep revealed BotManager.set_connector() was called in exactly
  ONE place in the entire codebase: the API Tester tab's _do_connect
  method at main_window.py:819. The Connect button on that tab
  was the only thing that hooked up the BotManager's connector
  reference and the History tab's callback.

  The normal production flow — clicking Start on a bot in the
  Trading tab — invokes _connect_exchange_for_bot (also in
  main_window.py around line 2304). That method:
    - creates a CCXTConnector
    - calls sync_connect to authenticate
    - fetches initial balance
    - assigns connector to bot.exchange
    - stores connector in self._exchange_connectors[eid]

  But it NEVER called self._bot_manager.set_connector(...). Never
  called connector.add_scan_symbol(...). Never called
  connector.set_history_callback(...).

  Three separate omissions in the same flow:
    1. BotManager._connector stays None → refresh_trade_history
       method at bot_container.py:596 logs "no connector attached"
       and silently returns. History Refresh button is inert.
    2. trade-historian background thread has no registered symbols
       → it hits the "no symbols registered — skipping auto-scan"
       early-return at ccxt_connector.py line 430 every time it
       fires. No scans ever happen.
    3. connector has no history callback → even if scans did happen,
       _on_history_result has no on_history_ready callable to
       dispatch completed analyses to the UI.

  Net effect: History tab was inert for anyone who started bots
  the normal way. The only users who could see it work were those
  who first went to API Tester → Connect before starting bots — an
  undocumented coupling.

FIX:

  Three additive calls in _connect_exchange_for_bot, right after
  `bot.exchange = connector`. Wrapped in try/except so any wiring
  failure never breaks bot-start:

      try:
          if hasattr(self, '_bot_manager') and self._bot_manager:
              self._bot_manager.set_connector(connector)
          connector.add_scan_symbol(bot.config.symbol)
          if (hasattr(self, '_trade_history_tab')
                  and self._trade_history_tab is not None):
              connector.set_history_callback(
                  self._trade_history_tab.get_history_callback())
      except Exception as _exc:
          logger.debug("MEM-222 history wiring failed: %s", _exc)

  Placeholder text in trade_history_tab.py updated from
  "No data — connect to an exchange" to
  "No data — start a bot to begin scanning" for accuracy.

REGRESSION GUARDS:

  9 new MEM-222 tests:
    - All three wiring calls present in _connect_exchange_for_bot
    - Wiring is wrapped in try/except
    - API Tester path preserved (existing coupling not broken)
    - set_connector() call sites is EXACTLY 2 (API Tester + MEM-222)
      — catches accidental duplication or accidental removal

WHY THE CALL-SITE COUNT INVARIANT MATTERS:

  If a future refactor adds a THIRD set_connector() call, we may
  double-wire and overwrite a working connector with a fresh one.
  If a refactor REMOVES one of the two, History tab goes dead
  again. Pinning the count at 2 catches both failure modes at
  test time.

MEM-224 — MEM-210 ROOT CAUSE: _parse_order OrderType(None) throws
          POST-TRADE-SUBMISSION. "BUY FAILED" WAS A LIE FOR WEEKS.
================================================================================

FORENSIC SUMMARY:

  Operator reported: "It fucking bought BONK. Why." after depositing USD
  and creating a CHIP bot. First theory (wrong): wizard symbol corruption.
  Second theory (wrong): BONK bot double-firing initial entry. Third theory
  (also wrong, proposed by Claude, rebuked by operator): outside deposit.

  Correct theory, found by reading the uploaded system.log line-by-line:
  every "BUY FAILED: VolumeGuard execution failed: None is not a valid
  OrderType" error in the log was a SUCCESSFUL real-money trade that
  executed on Coinbase. The exception was raised inside _parse_order,
  AFTER create_order had returned a successful response dict.

  16+ RAVE trades. 4+ phantom BONK trades. 1 BONK sell at 04:21. 1 BONK
  buy at 07:05. All executed. All reported as failures. All invisible to
  the bot's internal state until reconcile_holdings caught the drift
  30-90 seconds later.

EVIDENCE CHAIN:

  1. Operator's log pattern, repeated 20+ times across the session:

       [INFO] VolumeGuard: BONK/USD not tradeable  low volume
       [INFO] [COINBASE] PLACE_ORDER | Execute SELL limit order for BONK/USD
              | Sending to exchange... | 0ms
       [ERROR] Bot 065c2ff7 sell failed: VolumeGuard execution failed:
              None is not a valid OrderType
       [WARNING] Bot 065c2ff7 balance drift (post_failure):
                 internal=34676285 exchange=33485541 drift=-1190744 resetting

     The PLACE_ORDER INFO is logged immediately BEFORE create_order is
     called. There is no matching ORDER_PLACED success line before the
     ERROR — because _parse_order throws before that log fires. The
     reconcile_holdings on the next tick shows exchange_units has
     decreased by exactly the intended sell amount. QED: the order
     went through.

  2. The drifts match the intents exactly:

       04:21:16  SELL 1,190,744 intended  →  drift -1,190,744 (match)
       07:05:42  BUY    729,077 intended  →  drift +729,077  (match)
       10:04:34  drift +34,055,727 BONK ≈ $220 (exactly target_balance
                                                 of a hedge_replenish buy)
       10:15:07  drift +28,448,205 BONK ≈ $184 (a partial fill on another
                                                 invisible buy)

  3. _parse_order source at src/exchange/ccxt_connector.py:1024 was:

       type=OrderType(raw.get("type", "limit")),

     The pattern raw.get(k, default) returns default ONLY when k is
     absent from the dict. When k is present with value None (the
     Coinbase behaviour for market orders), get() returns None, not the
     default. OrderType(None) throws ValueError.

  4. Execution order in ccxt_connector.place_order:

       line 934: raw = await self._call_sync(self._ex.create_order, ...)
                 ← order submitted, Coinbase responds with raw dict
       line 939: order = self._parse_order(raw)
                 ← this line throws. Exception propagates up. Caller
                   reports "failed". Reality: order already filled.

THE FIX:

  src/exchange/ccxt_connector.py:1020-1033 rewrote _parse_order to use
  `raw.get(k) or default` instead of `raw.get(k, default)` for side, type,
  and status fields. The `or` short-circuit passes any falsy value (None,
  "", 0) through to the documented default. Numeric fields already used
  the `or` pattern and were unaffected.

  Total change: ~3 lines of actual logic. Massive blast radius.

REGRESSION DEFENCE:

  tests/test_mem224_parse_order_none_tolerance.py — 10 tests:
  - type=None doesn't throw, falls through to LIMIT
  - side=None doesn't throw, falls through to BUY
  - status=None doesn't throw, falls through to OPEN
  - Empty strings fall through to defaults
  - Absent keys still fall through to defaults
  - Normal limit/market orders still parse correctly
  - "closed" still maps to FILLED (regression check)
  - Reproduction of the 04:21:17 Coinbase sell payload parses cleanly
  - AST forbidden-pattern guard: refuses to let any future edit
    reintroduce `OrderSide(raw.get("side", ...))` or similar

IMPLICATIONS FOR MEM-223 (OPERATOR LOG STAGING):

  The RAVE cycle operator log we built earlier (4 scrums, 22% drawdown
  absorbed, +41.6 RAVE accumulated, 4.9% cost basis improvement) is
  FACTUALLY ACCURATE but CAUSALLY WRONG. The bot did not execute a
  coordinated scrum-fold strategy. It placed orders, thought they failed,
  and learned about their success via drift detection. The strategic
  gate logic was firing correctly — it was the execution reporting that
  was broken.

  The forbidden-phrase test in test_operator_log_staging.py already
  prevents us from publishing "validated the strategy" or "fully proved"
  in Part VI §31. Now we know why that safeguard mattered even more than
  we realised. The operator log, when it finally publishes, must include
  this forensic history — anything less is dishonest, because the RAVE
  cycle data was collected by a broken bot that only coincidentally
  produced useful numbers.

  Epistemically: the strategy may still be sound (the ORDERS the gate
  logic generated were correct), but the implementation did not execute
  the strategy as designed. Any claim that relies on "multi-tick
  coordination between a buy and its associated fold position" is
  unsupported — the bot had amnesia of its own buys within seconds of
  placing them.

ACCOUNTABILITY — CLAUDE MADE THIS HARDER:

  Operator's session-long complaint: "It fucking bought BONK. Why."
  My first three hypotheses:
    1. Wizard symbol corruption (wrong — I was looking for dramatic)
    2. BONK bot double-firing initial entry via _current_holdings stale

  Same failure mode as MEM-220 — pattern matching on familiar shapes

  R68 holds across time but not across hypotheses. The lesson is to

MEM-226 — HARD EXCHANGE-BALANCE SAFETY ON INITIAL ENTRY
        THREE STACKED BUGS, THREE ATOMIC FIXES
================================================================================

OPERATOR REPORT (volcanic, verbatim):

  "ANOTHER hard safety violation found. I had the $220 already purchased
   for CHIP. Started the bot and it bought another $220. IT IS NOT
   CHECKING THE FUCKING CURRENT BALANCES AND I HAVE REPORTED THIS BEFORE.
   I AM ABOUT TO GO VOLCANIC."

CODE AUDIT FINDINGS (src/trading/scrumming_bot.py):

  Three distinct bugs, all in the zero-balance initial entry path, any
  one of which alone would be serious, stacked together producing the
  "target balance bought twice" failure mode:

  BUG A — Stale-state gate (line 405):
    The gate `if current_value < self._target_balance * 0.01` trusts
    self._current_holdings from bot init. Bot init (line 321) reads
    balance via async exchange.get_balance(target_asset), which returns
    a Balance(free=0.0, used=0.0, total=0.0) if the currency key is
    absent from the raw fetch_balance response. No live re-verification
    before firing a target-sized buy.

    The GUI connection path (main_window.py:2372) reads balance via
    sync _ccxt_sync.fetch_balance() and shows the correct value. The
    bot's async path reads via self._call_sync(self._ex.fetch_balance)
    — the same underlying method but through the MEM-220 serialization
    executor. Any divergence between these two paths (caching, race
    with Coinbase account settling, currency-key case mismatch,
    rate-limiter returning empty on throttle) produces a bot that
    thinks holdings=0 while reality is holdings=target.

  BUG B — No-update success path (lines 518-523):
    After _execute_buy succeeds, the code appends to self._main_lots
    but NEVER updates self._current_holdings. On the next tick,
    current_value = self._current_holdings * ticker.last still
    returns 0. Gate fires AGAIN. Initial entry fires a SECOND time
    before periodic reconcile catches up 30-90 seconds later.

    This matches the operator's earlier-session report: "the BONK
    bought its Target Balance twice in a row as if in a loop." Same
    mechanism. Different asset.

  BUG C — Fail-open verify:
    If any live re-verification were added, it must fail CLOSED. The
    natural try/except pattern in Python fails open unless explicitly
    coded otherwise.

THE FIXES:

  (1) src/trading/scrumming_bot.py:406-466 — insert pre-buy live
      exchange re-verify block. Re-fetch target_asset balance. If
      live_value >= target * 0.01, BLOCK, log prominently, reset
      internal state to exchange truth, seed main_lots from reality,
      return WITHOUT firing buy.

  (2) src/trading/scrumming_bot.py:518-539 — update self._current_holdings
      atomically with _main_lots.append after successful entry. Two-line
      change; prevents next-tick re-fire.

  (3) Within the verify block, except Exception → log DEFERRED, return.
      No proceed path.

TESTS (tests/test_mem226_hard_exchange_safety.py — 8 source-level):

  - scrumming_bot.py parses
  - Pre-buy exchange-verify block is present + queries target_asset
  - Fail-closed on verify exception (DEFERRED + return)
  - Resets internal state to match exchange on mismatch
  - Success path updates _current_holdings (prevents re-fire loop)
  - BLOCKED path returns before any buy execution
  - Gate compares against live exchange balance, not stale internal
  - All prior safety anchors still present (MEM-197/207/208/226)

WHY SEPARATE FROM MEM-224:

  MEM-224 fixed execution REPORTING. Orders were succeeding but
  _parse_order threw ValueError before the success line ran; callers
  interpreted this as failure. Real money moved, bot had amnesia.

  MEM-226 fixes gate LOGIC. The gate fires when it shouldn't (bug A)
  and the success path doesn't prevent re-firing (bug B). Even with
  MEM-224 making every order visibly succeed or fail, if the gate
  logic wants to fire a target-sized buy on top of an already-held
  target position, it still does.

  Both needed. Orthogonal domains. Shipped separately because
  bookkeeping atomicity matters for forensic clarity.

EVIDENCE CHAIN FOR THIS FIX:

  Cold code read of src/trading/scrumming_bot.py:316-323 (pre-fix):
    if not self._initialised:
        ticker = await self.exchange.get_ticker(symbol)
        ...
        balance = await self.exchange.get_balance(self.config.target_asset)
        self._current_holdings = balance.free
        self._initialised = True

  Cold code read of src/exchange/ccxt_connector.py:
    - Line 856-881 (get_balances): filters currencies where total <= 0
      (line 866: if total > 0)
    - Line 884-888 (get_balance): returns
      Balance(currency=currency, free=0.0, used=0.0, total=0.0)
      silently when currency absent from get_balances result

  Observable: a single get_balance() returning zero (for ANY reason —
  stale, filtered, racy) is immediately and permanently trusted by the
  bot init. No retry. No verification. No handshake. _initialised
  flag is set, bot proceeds with belief = 0.

  This is the generic "bot constantly rebuying target balance"
  mechanism operator has reported repeatedly — not specific to one
  asset or one session. The init belief of zero holds until
  _reconcile_interval ticks (default 20, ~10 minutes) pass and
  reconcile_holdings corrects it.

FIX:

  get_balance+assign with double-read handshake:

  1. await exchange.get_balance(target_asset) → _h1
  2. await asyncio.sleep(0.25)
  3. await exchange.get_balance(target_asset) → _h2
  4. Compare: if |_h1 - _h2| / max(_h1, _h2) <= 0.001
     → trust, set _current_holdings = _h2, mark _initialised
  5. Else log MISMATCH, return without _initialised, retry next tick
  6. Exception path: log FAILED, re-raise, run_loop handles

  Module-level import of asyncio added at line 39 — was missing
  despite the new code's dependency on asyncio.sleep. Caught via
  grep after writing. Operator explicitly flagged this as the
  recurring discipline failure ("you are failing to make sure things
  are not imported when needed"). Rule for future sessions:
  grep-before-use, always, before writing the reference. ast.parse
  does NOT catch missing imports (NameError is runtime).

WHAT THIS FIX DOES NOT ADDRESS:

  - Buy execution paths do not themselves re-verify exchange before

================================================================================

OPERATOR REQUEST (verbatim):

EXTENSION (operator-approved):

CRITICAL OPERATOR CONSTRAINT:
  "we do not want to prevent normal Target Balance growth so DO NOT
   force checks for organic, properly checked growth."

DESIGN GROUNDING:

  Read scrumming_bot.py for the paths that call _execute_buy:
    - Line 560:  zero_balance_initial_entry
    - Line 1313: fold_rebuy
    - Line 1482: hedge_replenish

  Read where _target_balance mutates:
    - Line 106:  self._target_balance = config.target_balance (init)
    - Line 1375: self._target_balance += accum_profit (AFTER fold rebuy,
                 per profit-folding active — this is Shannon's Demon
                 compound growth, the core mechanism)

  Read hedge_replenish gate (line 1468-1475):
    - Fires only when delta < 0 (holdings BELOW target)
    - _use = min(self._hedge_bal * 0.5, _gap) — capped at the gap
    - Structurally cannot exceed target under correct operation

  Conclusion: fold_rebuy is the ONLY path where the buy is meant to
  coincide with target growth. Gating it would block the mechanism
  the operator specifically asked to preserve. Hedge replenish is
  structurally bounded. Initial entry and generic ceiling breaches
  are the only dangerous cases.

    - _BuyConfirmationBroker(QObject): bridge between bot async task
      and GUI main thread. Exposes async request_confirmation().

      buttons. WindowStaysOnTop flag so it can't be missed.
    - get_broker(): process-wide singleton factory.

    - After MEM-205 BUY TRACE log

    - Four branches based on trace_context["path"]:
        zero_balance_initial_entry  → always confirm
        fold_rebuy                  → never confirm
        hedge_replenish             → confirm only if projected > ceiling
        else                        → confirm only if projected > ceiling
    - Fail-closed on broker exception (return None)

  src/gui/main_window.py.MainWindow.__init__:
    - Initializes broker on GUI main thread so its receiving slot
      runs there (Qt.AutoConnection queues cross-thread emits correctly).

THREAD SAFETY (MEM-221 PATTERN REUSED):

  Bot thread:    creates Future on its event loop, emits Signal, awaits
  Signal hops:   Qt.AutoConnection queues to main thread event loop
  Main thread:   slot receives signal, constructs modal, .exec() blocks
                 main thread until user clicks
  Click handler: resolves Future on bot's loop via
                 loop.call_soon_threadsafe(fut.set_result, answer)
  Bot thread:    awaits Future returns answer; proceeds or refuses

  60-second timeout via asyncio.wait_for; on timeout Future is
  cancelled and we return "timeout" which is treated as refuse.

SESSION 24 ADDENDUM 5 (2026-04-22, 20:55 UTC)
MEM-229 — TOKEN TIMERS (SADP metabolism layer)
================================================================================

OPERATOR PROMPT (verbatim):
  "SADP - Upgrade (Possible) - Meditate on this and see if you get
   where i am going....Token Timers."

CLAUDE MEDITATION:

  SADP rules today are triggered by events (cascade close, hop open,
  classifier hits) or by mtimes (file X older than file Y). What they
  don't measure is drift over effort — the state where too much work
  has accumulated since the last grounding check without an intervening
  consultation of the rules.

  This same session violated R68 three times. Each violation came AFTER
  I had drifted from the rules without a re-read between speculative
  fixes. No single event crossed a threshold; it was accumulation that
  did the damage.

  Token Timers close that gap. They measure elapsed EVENTS since a
  grounding — where events proxy for tokens, because I cannot read my
  own token count, but the count between groundings correlates with
  ungrounded effort.

IMPLEMENTATION:

  sadp/token_timer.py (380 lines):
    - record(kind, meta) — append to TOKEN_TIMER_LOG.jsonl
    - read_journal(since_session_start=True) — session-scoped read
    - 5 check functions returning CheckResult
    - CLI: --record, --check, --journal

  Valid event kinds:
    rule_read, cold_read, hypothesis_proposed, fix_shipped,
    fix_reverted, operator_correction, session_start, session_end

  Invalid kinds raise ValueError (R28 FL).

  Session scoping: read_journal filters to events AFTER the most
  recent session_start, so cross-session state doesn't bleed into
  current-session checks.

THE FIVE CHECKS (all session-scoped):

  TT-001 rule_freshness — >8 events since last rule_read
  TT-002 hypothesis_grounding — most recent hypothesis_proposed
         has no intervening cold_read (ungrounded pattern-matching)
  TT-003 speculation_gate — fix_shipped count exceeds cold_read count
  TT-004 reversion_pressure — >=2 reverts since last rule_read
  TT-005 correction_cluster — >=2 operator_corrections in last 5 events

  TT-003/004/005 block cascades. TT-001/002 are advisory (visible in
  dashboard but won't halt a ship).

INTEGRATION WITH CHECKLIST.json:

  Added CHK-020 through CHK-024 — five new items using the new
  'token_timer' custom handler. Each specifies tt_check=<name>;
  the handler delegates to the specific check function.

  Total checklist items: 19 → 24.

WHY EVENT COUNT PROXIES TOKEN COUNT:

  Token count would be the ideal unit — but I cannot read my own
  context token consumption. What I CAN count is meaningful events:
  code I read, fixes I shipped, operator corrections I received,
  rules I re-consulted.

  The quantity Token Timers want to measure is 'how much un-grounded
  effort has accumulated.' Event count between groundings correlates
  with that directly. A session that shipped 3 speculative fixes with
  no intervening rule_read has a drift problem regardless of whether
  the tokens between were 15K or 50K.

  - Session scoping

  - CLI --check produces valid JSON

SEEDED STATE FOR CURRENT SESSION:

================================================================================

OPERATOR PROMPT (verbatim):

CLAUDE MEDITATION:

  MEM-229 gave Token Timers a metabolism, but it was a crude one: flat
  budgets, uniform event cost. A speculative fix in src/trading/
  scrumming_bot.py weighed the same as a typo fix in CHANGELOG.md.
  Real drift is context-dependent — edits to trading-core code are
  categorically more dangerous than docs edits, and the budget should
  reflect that.

  The operator's second concern was subtler: without a floor, adverse
  context could scale a rule's budget toward zero, making it
  effectively impossible to fail. A "rule that never fires" is not a
  rule. Non-Zero Protection guarantees a rule always has enough budget
  to eventually demand refresh.

DESIGN (operator-pinned):

  A1: All three layers — file-path default × event-kind modulator,
      explicit tag overrides.
  A2: Percentage floor (40% of base) — self-scaling.

IMPLEMENTATION:

    - floor_pct: 0.40
    - default_file_weight: 1.0
    - file_path_weights: 23 entries spanning trading-core (3.0),
      exchange-core (2.8), core (1.8), gui-critical (1.5),
      sadp-core (1.5), tests (0.8), docs (0.3)
    - event_kind_modulators: rule_read 1.0, cold_read 1.0,
      hypothesis_proposed 1.2, fix_shipped 1.5, fix_reverted 2.5,
      operator_correction 3.0
    - explicit_tag_weights: safety-critical 4.0, money-flow 3.5,
      cosmetic 0.2, whitespace 0.1
    - rule_overrides: TT-001 tightens on trading-core (0.5),
      loosens on docs (2.0)

  sadp/token_timer.py additions:
    - load_weights_config() — fail-safe loader (returns {} on error)
    - compute_event_weight(event, cfg) — three-layer resolution
    - weighted_events_since, weighted_count_kind, context_tags_since_last
    - effective_budget_for_rule(rule, base, tags, cfg) — applies
      context multiplier AND floor: max(base*mult, base*floor_pct)
    - check_rule_freshness upgraded: uses weighted path when cfg
      loaded, falls back to flat count when cfg absent

BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY:

  Critical property: when PROJECT_WEIGHTS.json is missing OR malformed,
  every weighted helper returns 1.0 per event and every check falls
  back to its original count-based semantics. Original 16 Token Timer
  tests pass unchanged. This was verified with:
    - test_no_config_file_check_passes_unweighted
    - test_corrupt_config_falls_back_safely

NON-ZERO PROTECTION PROOF:

  test_floor_never_reaches_zero feeds an adversarial context with
  multiplier 0.0 and asserts effective_budget == base * 0.40.
  The floor holds: rule_id TT-001 with base 8 and a 0.0 multiplier
  still ends up with effective budget 3.2, not 0. The rule CANNOT
  be weighted into non-existence.

TT-001 END-TO-END DEMONSTRATION:

    → 0.9 < 16.0 → PASS

  Same rule, same number of events, radically different outcome

================================================================================

OPERATOR EVIDENCE:
  Screenshot of Bot Settings dialog for running BONK/USD bot on v3.15.10.
  Settings tab showed: Order Visibility, Check Interval, Aggressive,
  Bulk, Scrumming Interval, BB Tolerance, Landing Strip, TA TF,

  Wizard has ~20 fields including all 6 P1.9 advanced, both hedge
  fields, plus the whole phantom subsystem. Parity gap was about 11
  fields and one entire tab.

  Operator directive: "This needs a Phantom Bot tab and all settings
  from the New Bot configuration screen."

DESIGN DECISIONS:

  P1.9 fields + Hedge fields: these already live on BotConfig (since
  v3.13.8 MEM-182). The live dialog just wasn't exposing them. Adding
  them is pure UI — _mark_changed writes to config, _apply_changes
  setattr's the config. Works for free.

  Phantom fields: DON'T live on BotConfig. They're runtime attrs
  (_phantoms_enabled, _phantom_timeframes) plus coordinator state
  (_coordinator.lock_candle_count). Options considered:

    A. Plumb phantom fields onto BotConfig, setattr like the others.
       Pros: uniform. Cons: wire changes across bot construction,
       restoration from state, and the bot itself reading them.
       Biggest risk: config-sourced phantoms and bot-runtime phantoms
       would have two sources of truth for the TF list.

    B. New method on ScrummingBot (update_phantom_config) that
       handles the runtime writes. _apply_changes routes phantom
       fields there instead of setattr'ing config.
       Pros: isolates phantom-specific logic (MEM-203 filter at
       update time, caveats about existing-phantom lifecycle).
       Cons: _apply_changes branches.

  Chose B. The caveats are material — you can't just flip
  _phantoms_enabled mid-session and have existing phantoms stop
  cleanly (requires async unwind). The method returns a caveats[]
  list so the UI can log them, which structurally acknowledges the
  lifecycle constraint instead of pretending it doesn't exist (R28 FL).

  src/gui/bot_live_settings.py:
    - Settings tab gets "Advanced Scrumming (P1.9)" group

    - Settings tab gets "Hedge Rebalance" group (active, balance)
    - New tab "Phantom Bot" via _create_phantom_tab (scrumming only)
    - _mark_changed branches on field name — phantom fields compare
      against bot runtime attrs not bot.config
    - _apply_changes partitions pending changes into phantom + other;
      phantom changes → bot.update_phantom_config(), others → setattr

  src/trading/scrumming_bot.py:
    - New method update_phantom_config(enable_phantoms=None,
      phantom_timeframes=None, lock_candle_count=None)
    - Returns {"applied": dict, "caveats": list}
    - MEM-203 unsupported-TF filter applied at update time too
    - Enable/disable caveats: existing phantoms keep running until
      restart; new phantoms respect the new flag
    - TF set changes apply to new phantoms only
    - lock_candle_count writes to self._coordinator immediately

OPERATOR EVIDENCE:

  Three constraints:
    1. Insectoid — locust specifically
    2. 30% smaller
    3. NO dangled functionality (Smart Wire called out by name)

APPROACH (first-principles per R68):

  Step 1: Read the full paintEvent to enumerate the functional
  contract. Catalogued 10 data surface fields and 4 API methods.
  Every one must survive the rewrite.

  Step 2: Read the Smart Wire path. _get_bot_center uses
  widget.width()/2, widget.height()/2 as wire anchor. _bot_at_pos
  uses widget.rect().contains() for hit testing. These don't care
  about the widget's internal design — they care about the widget's
  GEOMETRIC center and BOUNDING RECT. Both preservable.

  Step 3: Design the locust so its thorax (visual body center) lands
  at (w/2, h/2). Smart Wire keeps working without any changes to
  the parent tab.

  Step 4: Map every data field to anatomy. This is where the "don't
  dangle functionality" constraint binds hardest — not a single data
  field can become invisible. Mapping:
    - Head + compound eye → state (preattentive focus per Knaflic)
    - Thorax → symbol + mode badge (armored plate at visual center)
    - Segmented abdomen → P/L gauge (log-scaled magnitude)
    - Wings → state + trade pulse (posture-driven)
    - Legs (3 pairs, hind thick+bent) → ambient locust signature
    - Antennae → price tick sway (ambient life)

  Found a container override at BotVisualizationTab.update_bots
  line ~1881 — node.setMinimumSize(280, 240) — which was sized for
  the OLD 320x280 widget plus ~25% padding. If left in place it
  would have BLOCKED the 30% shrink because Qt takes the MAX of
  both setMinimumSize calls. Removed it; widget's own __init__
  minimum is authoritative. This is exactly the kind of "parent
  fights child" bug P-007 pathology guards against.

  ground in project canon. Cited six authorities from VISUAL_CRAFT:

        Layer 1 CRACK (6ms):
          - White noise with running-mean HPF (prev = 0.85*prev + 0.15*wn)
          - Fast attack-decay envelope: 1 - sqrt(i/n)
          - High-freq filtered band

          - exp(-6t) envelope across the 120ms
        Layer 4 TAIL (260ms):

      - All layers concat, clip to [-1, 1], multiply by

SESSION 24 ADDENDUM 13 (2026-04-23, 02:30 UTC)
MEM-238 — COINS-IN-BUCKET (PROFIT) + WATER DRIP (ACCUMULATION) SFX
================================================================================

OPERATOR DIRECTIVE:
  "New sounds: Coins dropping into a bucket for P/L increases.
   Dripping water for accumulation."

GROUNDING (R68, R69):
  Re-read sadp/AUDIO_CRAFT.md conventions for reserved names and
  frequency band assignments. Verified:
    - Existing reserved names: buy, sell, error, state, track, fire
    - Free bands: HIGH (5-12kHz), some of MID, LOW-MID, LOW
    - Existing trigger surface: _on_trade_filled_sfx in main_window.py
    - Pattern for new SFX: _gen_X helper in sound_engine + play_X
      convenience + SoundConfig field + play() gate

SOUND DESIGN:

  COINS-IN-BUCKET (profit):
    Physical model: a coin striking another coin/metal surface then
    settling in a hollow container.
    - Tink (2ms): HF noise burst, captures the sharp contact moment.
      HPF implemented as: hp = wn - prev_running_mean.
    - Ring (140ms): two sines detuned ~60Hz apart around 2.4-2.9kHz,
      exp(-14t) decay. The beat frequency produced by detuning is
      what makes brass sound like brass rather than a pure tone.
    - Body (80ms): two close sines at ~380Hz + harmonic, exp(-22t)
      decay. The bucket's hollow thunk.
    - Three coins staggered 0/135/280ms, each slightly randomized in
      frequency and amplitude. Second coin catches first's ring
      tail for characteristic "jingly" overlap.
    Total 500ms, ~22KB @ 22050Hz mono 16-bit.

  WATER DRIP (drip):
    Physical model: water drop impacting a surface.
    - Impact (1.5ms): brief noise burst. Just enough transient to
      sound like the drop landing.
    - Cavity ploink (55ms): this is the SIGNATURE. A single sine
      with EXPONENTIAL frequency sweep from 1400Hz down to 800Hz.
      Physically: when a drop hits water, a small air bubble briefly
      forms and collapses; the oscillation frequency falls as the
      cavity shrinks. Without this sweep it would sound like a
      generic tonk. WITH the sweep it's unmistakably water.
      Implementation: phase integration (phase += 2*pi*f_now/sr per
      sample) rather than computing f*t with variable f — the
      latter produces phase discontinuities.
    - Ring tail (100ms): soft 800Hz residue, exp(-28t). The final
      cavity resonance decays.
    Total 200ms, ~9KB.

ROUTING DECISIONS:

  Coins on profit > 0 — fires on any trade event (grid or scrumming)
  that realized profit. Generic enough to be useful across bot modes.

  Drip on FOLD only — "accumulation" in Acervator has a specific
  meaning (MEM-171: units gained by buying back more asset than was
  sold at a lower price). That happens on FOLD. SCRUM and DIST are
  direction conversions, not accumulation events. Keeping this
  specific prevents audio fatigue and preserves the drip as a
  meaningful signal.

  All three trade-related SFX (rifle, coins, drip) can fire
  simultaneously on one FOLD event with profit > 0. Bregman-separated
  bands ensure they layer cleanly:
    - Rifle: low + broadband noise
    - Coins: high ring + mid brass + low-mid body
    - Drip: mid sweep
  No stagger needed.

SETTINGS INTEGRATION:

  Followed the MEM-236 pattern exactly: QCheckBox per sound, Test
  button per sound, _on_sfx_volume_changed updated to forward new
  fields when rebuilding SoundConfig. No new code paths — the volume
  slider's existing cache-invalidate logic handles regen.

AUDIO_CRAFT MAINTENANCE (R69 IN PRACTICE):

  The anchor was created yesterday (MEM-237). Today's cascade extends
  both the feature AND the anchor in the same ship. This is R69
  working as designed: knowledge anchors are LIVE documents that
  grow with the feature surface. Future sessions reading AUDIO_CRAFT
  will see all 8 reserved names with full provenance.

TESTING DISCIPLINE:

  Envelope tests for both sounds use actual synthesis → WAV →
  struct.unpack → RMS window analysis. Not AST checks on source
  strings. The 3-peak test for coins and monotonic-decay test for
  drip validate the FINAL OUTPUT, not the implementation. If the
  coin synthesis ever degrades (e.g., a layer's envelope shape is
  accidentally inverted), the test catches it regardless of code
  structure.

SESSION 24 ADDENDUM 14 (2026-04-23, 03:00 UTC)
MEM-239 — FIRE BUTTON GLOWS WHEN ARMED AND READY
================================================================================

OPERATOR DIRECTIVE:
  "Fire buttons we added should glow red when ARMED and READY."

GROUNDING (R68):
  Cold-read of BotStatusTable.update_bots (the MEM-236 Fire button
  creation block) and _setup_pulse / _pulse_tick (the existing
  pulse-animation infrastructure on stat cards). Key findings:

    1. scrum_target_mode is already exposed in status dicts by
       MEM-236. No new data plumbing needed.
    2. Existing _pulse_timer ticks at 80ms using QGraphicsOpacityEffect.
       Reusing this tick for glow animation avoids adding a second
       timer.
    3. Qt QSS does NOT support CSS animations (@keyframes, animation:
       property). Must use QGraphicsDropShadowEffect for a real glow.
    4. BotStatusTable.update_bots runs per refresh — recreates widgets.
       Any effect attached to a widget becomes a dangling reference
       when that widget is reused / destroyed. Registry must prune.

INTERPRETATION:
  "ARMED and READY" maps cleanly to scrum_target_mode == "fire". The
  FIRE phase is the bot's final pre-fire state — all gate conditions
  have been met on the active band, and the next qualifying tick
  executes the trade. That's the moment the button should draw the
  eye.

  Deliberately added an intermediate TRACK tier (amber, no glow)
  because the tracking-beep cadence already distinguishes these
  three phases audibly (silent / slow / fast). Adding visual parity
  on the Fire button means the operator gets the SAME three-phase
  signal through two senses. Bregman-auditory-scene-analysis-style
  separation (MEM-237) translates to visual separation cleanly.

IMPLEMENTATION:

  BotStatusTable.update_bots (Fire button creation, col 7):
    - Read scrum_phase = status.get("scrum_target_mode")
    - Enabled branch splits three ways on scrum_phase
    - FIRE: full visual treatment — bg #d61a3d, border 1px #ff3366,
      white bold text, QGraphicsDropShadowEffect blur 18 color
      #ff3366 offset 0,0, registered with main window
    - TRACK: amber #ffaa00 bold text, no bg, no glow
    - SEARCH/None (else): prior #ff3366 subdued text

  Main window:
    - _setup_pulse gains self._fire_glow_effects: list = []
    - _register_fire_glow(effect): prunes dead effects (probe with
      .blurRadius(); RuntimeError = deleted Qt object), then appends
      the new effect
    - _pulse_tick extended: glow_blur = 17.0 + 5.0 * sin(phase * 1.6);
      multiplier 1.6 on the phase gives the glow a faster throb than
      the base opacity pulse. Also prunes dead glows mid-tick if
      setBlurRadius raises.

  Best-effort registration:
    - Table uses self.window() to reach main window
    - hasattr(_root, "_register_fire_glow") gates the call
    - Whole glow creation block wrapped in try/except so legacy /
      test contexts don't crash if QGraphicsDropShadowEffect unavailable

TOOLTIP LANGUAGE (operator-facing):
  FIRE:  "ARMED — bot is in FIRE phase, scrum gate conditions met on
          the active band. Clicking forces immediate evaluation on the
          next tick."
  TRACK: "TRACKING — bot detected band approach and is aiming. Fire
          will force early evaluation."
  SEARCH:"Force immediate scrum/fold evaluation on next tick. Does
          NOT bypass gate conditions."

  The ARMED tooltip is important — it tells the operator that the
  glow isn't decorative; the bot is AT the trigger, not approaching.

TESTS (tests/test_mem239_fire_glow_armed.py — 12 tests):
  - File parses
  - scrum_phase read from status dict
  - Three enabled tiers present (FIRE if / TRACK elif / else)
  - FIRE tier uses QGraphicsDropShadowEffect with red color and
    setBlurRadius + setGraphicsEffect
  - FIRE tier tooltip contains "ARMED"
  - TRACK tier uses amber #ffaa00 and "TRACKING" tooltip
  - _register_fire_glow method exists
  - _pulse_tick animates blur radius with sin-based oscillation
  - Registry prunes dead refs with RuntimeError catch on .blurRadius()
  - _pulse_tick also prunes dead glows and handles RuntimeError
  - Disabled tier unchanged (#555, scrumming-only tooltip)
  - Glow registration is best-effort (self.window() + hasattr gate +
    outer try/except)

SESSION 24 ADDENDUM 15 (2026-04-23, 03:30 UTC)
MEM-240 — BOT SETTINGS DIALOG INITIAL RENDER FIX
================================================================================

OPERATOR INPUT:
  Screenshot of Bot Settings dialog (BONK/USD, bot 6d832ef6) showing
  striped-band rendering where controls should have been. Title bar,
  header, tabs, and Hedge Rebalance group rendered correctly, but the
  other group boxes (Trading Parameters, Scrumming Settings, Advanced
  Scrumming P1.9) showed horizontal striped bands with labels
  clipped/overlapping.

OPERATOR QUOTE:
  "Initial appearance of the details windows. Not very useful. Pretty
   sure some GUI rules are broken here."

GROUNDING (R68):
  Cold-read of src/gui/bot_live_settings.py confirmed:
    - setMinimumSize(620, 580)
    - No QScrollArea anywhere
    - 4 QGroupBoxes on Settings tab, each with QFormLayout + multiple
      rows (verified by grep against addRow calls)
    - src/gui/settings_dialog.py already uses QScrollArea (lines
      649, 763) — precedent exists

  Content-height math:
    Trading Parameters: ~170px (4 rows + header + padding)
    Scrumming Settings: ~200px (5 rows)
    Advanced Scrumming:  ~260px (7 rows)
    Hedge Rebalance:     ~110px (2 rows)
    Plus header (~80px), info bar (~30px), buttons (~60px)
    Total: ~982px content vs 580px dialog min = ~402px overflow

  Why Hedge Rebalance rendered fine: only 2 rows, fit naturally
  within the compression headroom available.

  Why the striping: Qt's native widget paint code has minimum row
  heights (varies by platform/theme, ~22-28px). Below that, painters
  give up and draw a degenerate stripe rather than a full control.

FIX (THREE LAYERS):

  Layer 1: _wrap_scrollable(content: QWidget) -> QScrollArea
    - setWidgetResizable(True) so horizontal growth follows viewport
    - setFrameShape(QFrame.NoFrame) so scroll area is visually
      transparent
    - setWidget(content) to install the tab's existing widget
    - Applied to all four addTab sites (Status, Settings, Phantom Bot,
      Adjust Stack)
    - Tab factory methods unchanged — they still return QWidget;
      wrapping is localized to the dialog's tab-registration section

  Layer 2: setMinimumSize(640, 720)
    - Raised from (620, 580) so common case fits most of Settings tab
      without needing the scroll bar
    - 720px still fits 1080p screens (900+ usable after taskbar/titlebar)

  Layer 3: _configure_form(form: QFormLayout)
    - fieldGrowthPolicy=AllNonFixedFieldsGrow: field widgets expand
      horizontally, labels stay at natural width
    - rowWrapPolicy=DontWrapRows: labels and fields always on same line
    - setHorizontalSpacing(12), setVerticalSpacing(8): generous
      breathing room between labels and fields
    - setContentsMargins(8, 8, 8, 8): group-internal padding
    - Applied to all 10 QFormLayouts via regex auto-injection:
        re.sub(r'^(\s+)(\w+) = QFormLayout\([^)]+\)',
               lambda m: m.group(0) + '\n' + m.group(1) +
                        f'self._configure_form({m.group(2)})', ...)
    - This is belt-and-suspenders: even if the scroll wrap is ever
      removed, rows can't collapse into stripe territory

REGRESSION CAUGHT:
  tests/test_mem232_phantom_tab.py had:
    assert "addTab(self._create_phantom_tab()" in src
  which failed once the addTab call became:
    tabs.addTab(self._wrap_scrollable(
        self._create_phantom_tab()), "Phantom Bot")
  Updated the assertion to accept either direct or scroll-wrapped form.
  This is a true test maintenance update, not a weakening — the test
  still verifies phantom-tab registration is scrumming-gated.

WHAT THE OPERATOR WILL SEE:
  Open any Bot Settings dialog on v3.15.22:
    - All control rows render as actual QDoubleSpinBox / QComboBox /
      QCheckBox widgets, not stripe patterns
    - Settings tab shows natural spacing between rows
    - If the dialog is resized smaller than ~720px tall, a scroll
      bar appears on the right of the content area — no clipping
    - Group boxes maintain natural heights regardless of dialog size

SCOPE DISCIPLINE (R64 FCP):
  One production file touched (bot_live_settings.py). One test

SESSION 24 ADDENDUM 17 (2026-04-23, 05:00 UTC)
MEM-242 — MANUAL FIRE PLUMBING BUGFIX
================================================================================

OPERATOR REPORT:
  "Manual Fire button plumbing is busted. Only get a message and no
   follow through or kaboom."

GROUNDING (R68 — First Principles):
  Operator's symptom had a clear pattern: message shown (so click
  reached bot), no trade executed (so rebalance didn't run). Two
  possible regions to audit: the tick() entry where _manual_fire_pending
  is checked, OR the _execute_manual_rebalance method itself.

  Read cold in this order:
    1. scrumming_bot.py __init__: verified flag init
    2. force_fire(): verified flag set + counter bump
    3. tick() lines 451-490: FOUND BUG 1 (skip-gate recomputes skip
       from config; counter bump becomes stale on mode change)
    4. tick() manual-fire branch lines 637-652: structure OK but no
       entry diagnostic (BUG 3)
    5. _execute_manual_rebalance: FOUND BUG 2 (filled=0.0 truthiness)

THE THREE BUGS:

  BUG 1 — Root cause. Read-rate tick-skip race.
  ----------------------------------------------
  tick() recomputes _tick_skip every call:
    _base_skip = int((scrum_read_rate_min * 60) / tick_interval)
    if scrum_target_mode in ('track', 'fire'):
        _tick_skip = _base_skip // 10  # small (e.g. 6)
    else:
        _tick_skip = _base_skip        # full (e.g. 60)

  force_fire did: _tick_counter = max(_tick_counter, _tick_skip - 1)
  assuming _tick_skip was stable. If bot was in TRACK mode when
  operator pressed Fire (_tick_skip=6), counter became 5. But before
  next tick the bot dropped to SEARCH (_tick_skip recomputed to 60),
  counter bumped to 6 in skip check, `6 < 60` True → return.

  Result: operator waits up to (60-6) × 5s = 270s = 4.5 minutes.

  Fix: gate condition extended to `and not self._manual_fire_pending`.
  Plus an elif branch that resets counter so polling restarts cleanly
  after the override runs.

  BUG 2 — Truthiness trap on Order.filled.
  -----------------------------------------
  `if order is None or not getattr(order, "filled", None):`

  For MARKET orders, some exchanges populate:
    filled = 0.0   ← falsey!
    amount = actual_fill
    average = actual_avg_price

  Python's truthiness: `not 0.0` is True. Legitimate fill → abort.

  Fix: explicit extraction with fallback chain + explicit comparison:
    _filled_raw = getattr(o, "filled") or getattr(o, "amount") or requested
    fill_amount = float(_filled_raw or 0.0)
    if fill_amount <= 0: abort

  BUG 3 — Observability gap.
  --------------------------
  Symptom "only a message" could mean:
    (a) tick never ran the check — skip gate blocked it
    (b) check ran but rebalance returned early — dust band / zero amount
    (c) rebalance crashed and caught exception but no log

  The existing logs distinguished (b) and (c) but not (a). Added an
  entry log BEFORE the rebalance call that prints holdings, price,
  target. If operator ever presses Fire again and doesn't see this log,
  the bug is back in the tick-skip region and not in the rebalance
  method itself.

TESTS (tests/test_mem242_manual_fire_plumbing.py — 8 tests):
  - File parses
  - Skip gate includes "not self._manual_fire_pending" clause
  - Manual fire bypass elif resets counter
  - Diagnostic entry log with holdings/price/target before rebalance
  - Both branches use explicit fill_amount check with fallback chain
  - fill_price uses fallback chain (average_price → average → price)
  - Distinct log messages for order=None vs fill=0 cases
  - Structural order preserved (skip → init → manual fire check)

DISCIPLINE:
  Single-file fix. TT-001 tripped on trading-core tag (weight 4.5 vs
  budget 4.0), re-grounded before ship. No new parity debt.

SESSION 24 ADDENDUM 18 (2026-04-23, 05:30 UTC)
MEM-243 — MANUAL FIRE FOLD BALANCE FETCH BUGFIX
================================================================================

OPERATOR OUTPUT:
  [20:37:45] MANUAL FIRE FOLD: delta=-$5.9833 but USD free=$0.0000.
             Cannot rebalance.

Operator's account is funded. The zero was a bug.

GROUNDING (R68):
  The diagnostic log from MEM-242 PROVED the tick reached the
  rebalance entry (otherwise there'd be no MANUAL FIRE FOLD message
  at all). So the bug was inside _execute_manual_rebalance, not in
  the tick plumbing.

  Read cold:
    1. grep for get_balance signatures across exchange/ module
    2. Exchange interface: `get_balance(self, currency: str) -> Balance`
       (REQUIRED currency arg, returns Balance dataclass)
    3. Exchange also has: `get_balances() -> dict[str, Balance]`
       (no-arg bulk form)
    4. Existing scrumming_bot code uses:
       - `get_balance(self.config.target_asset)` in init handshake
       - `.free` attribute access on the Balance object
    5. My rebalance code: `get_balance()` with no arg, `.get("USD",
       {}).get("free")` dict-style access
       → raises TypeError → caught by bare except → silent 0.0

  This is pathology P-008: caller misreads callee contract. Bare
  except Exception: swallowed the TypeError, producing a silent
  failure mode that looked like "no USD in account."

THREE FIX IMPROVEMENTS:

  (1) Derive quote_currency from symbol
      ------------------------------------
      quote_currency = self.config.symbol.split("/")[-1]

      Works for BONK/USD → "USD", SOL/USDT → "USDT", WIF/USDC →
      "USDC", DOGE/EUR → "EUR", etc. Original hardcoded "USD" would
      have been wrong for non-USD pairs even if the dict access had
      worked.

  (2) Call get_balance with currency argument + .free attribute
      -----------------------------------------------------------
      bal = await self.exchange.get_balance(quote_currency)
      usd_balance = float(getattr(bal, "free", 0) or 0)

      Matches the interface contract. getattr with default=0 is
      defensive in case the Balance implementation is subclassed
      without the attribute.

  (3) Fallback chain to get_balances() dict
      --------------------------------------
      except Exception as exc:
          _bal_err = exc
          balances = await self.exchange.get_balances()
          b = balances.get(quote_currency)
          if b is not None:
              usd_balance = float(getattr(b, "free", 0) or 0)

      If single-currency call raises (auth issue, exchange quirk),
      try the bulk form. If both fail, _bal_err carries the last
      exception and the log surfaces it.

  (4) Dynamic currency name in log messages
      --------------------------------------
      Replaced hardcoded "USD" with f"{quote_currency}" in the
      cannot-rebalance log and CLIPPED-by log. A USDT bot now says
      "USDT free=$X" not "USD free=$X".

TESTS (tests/test_mem243_balance_fetch.py — 9 tests):
  - File parses
  - Buggy no-arg pattern + dict access removed
  - Quote currency derived from symbol split
  - get_balance called with currency arg
  - Uses Balance.free attribute access (not dict .get)
  - Fallback to get_balances() dict present
  - Log surfaces fetch error on failure
  - Log messages use dynamic quote_currency
  - Defensive meta-test: inspect.signature(ExchangeInterface.get_balance)
    catches future interface refactors

DISCIPLINE:
  TT-001 tripped on trading-core tag weight 4.5 vs budget 4.0 — same
  pattern as MEM-242. Re-grounded before ship. The operator gave me
  the exact bug diagnostic and I found the root cause in the first
  cold-read pass. This is what observability-driven bugfixing feels
  like: the log pointed at the bug, the cold read confirmed it, the
  fix was surgical.

MEM-244 — POSITION CEILING + DETONATION (INSTITUTIONAL RISK CONTROLS)
================================================================================

OPERATOR DIRECTIVE:
  Emerged from a conversation about RAVE accumulation. Operator moved
  from "no ceiling, farm until raisins" to "probably 2 or 3x" when I
  pushed back on unbounded conviction positioning. That became:
    "Maybe make that a switch. Institutions are going to want it for
     sure. 1x~10x should be reasonable. Bot should detonate on 1D or
     higher Timeframe on BULLISH condition detection."

  Two distinct features clearly:
    1. Position Ceiling — cap accumulation at Nx of anchor
    2. Detonation — proactive harvest on higher-TF bullish confirm

DESIGN CLARIFICATIONS (via ask_user_input, five questions total):
  Q1 (anchor):   Initial target_balance frozen at creation
  Q2 (at cap):   Slow fold rate (taper approaching, hard-stop at 1.0)
  Q3 (harvest):  Sell everything above ANCHOR (not current target)
  Q4 (trigger):  BULLISH + confidence >= 0.75
  Q5 (reset):    Yes — reset target to anchor on detonation (full lock-in)

  The Q5 follow-up mattered because "sell everything above anchor"
  alone leaves target_balance elevated, which would cause the bot to
  immediately re-fold to restore delta. Operator chose full reset:
  harvest-and-restart semantics, re-accumulate from scratch on next
  dip. Cleanest mental model.

GROUNDING (R68 — First Principles):
  Cold-read BotConfig layout (fields run to line 138, __post_init__
  at 140). Found existing pattern: `aggressive_trading: bool = False`
  — so bool toggles with sensible defaults fit naturally. Config loader
  at line 752+ threads each field with cfg.get(key, default) fallback.
  
  VotingEngine already parsed in tick() init-gate block (line 770);
  same engine used for detonation TF check. candles_from_raw + 
  compute_all(parsed, tf) works uniformly for any TF string the 
  exchange supports.
  
  _execute_manual_rebalance (MEM-241) has the structural template for
  _execute_detonation — MARKET order via guarded_place_order, fill
  amount with fallback chain, decrement holdings, emit trade.filled.
  Key difference: detonation also mutates state (reset target, clear
  fold queue, reseed main_lots).

IMPLEMENTATION (4 files):

  src/trading/bot_container.py:
    - BotConfig: 5 new fields in a "MEM-244 Risk Controls" section
      with comprehensive docstring explaining the two toggles and
      their semantic
    - Config loader threads all 5 fields through cfg.get(...) with
      defaults matching the dataclass
    - get_status exposes 8 new keys for GUI consumption:
        anchor_target_balance, position_ceiling_enabled,
        position_ceiling_multiple, position_ceiling_usd,
        ceiling_ratio, fold_rate_taper,
        detonation_enabled, detonation_timeframe

  src/trading/scrumming_bot.py:
    - __init__: self._anchor_target_balance = float(config.target_balance)
      — captured once, never mutated after. Also state for edge-trigger:
      _detonation_last_check_ts, _detonation_last_signal_bullish.
    - @property position_ceiling_usd: None when disabled, else
      anchor * clamp(multiplier, 1.0, 10.0). Defensive clamp protects
      against bad saved config values.
    - @property ceiling_ratio: holdings*price / ceiling. None when
      disabled or no price.
    - @property fold_rate_taper: piecewise function:
        ratio < 0.5  → 1.0  (full rate, no taper)
        0.5 ≤ ratio < 1.0  → 1.0 - (ratio-0.5)/0.5 * 0.9  (linear 1.0→0.1)
        ratio ≥ 1.0  → 0.0  (hard stop)
        always 1.0 when ceiling disabled
    - async _check_detonation_trigger(ticker):
        * Gate 1: detonation_enabled
        * Gate 2: current_value > anchor (nothing to harvest below)
        * Gate 3: 1-hour rate limit on exchange fetch
        * Fetch higher-TF candles via exchange.get_ohlcv(symbol, tf, 100)
        * Run VotingEngine
        * fired = is_bullish AND NOT _detonation_last_signal_bullish
        * Update latched state
        * Returns True iff fired this call
        * Exception-safe (logs + returns False; will retry 1hr later)
    - async _execute_detonation(ticker):
        * Compute excess = current_value - anchor
        * MARKET sell excess/price asset via guarded_place_order
        * Fill fallback chain (filled / amount / requested) same as
          MEM-242 discipline
        * fill_price fallback (average_price / average / price)
        * Decrement holdings
        * RESET: target_balance = anchor, fold_tranches cleared,

          auto_detonated_reset: True}
        * Emit trade.filled type=AUTO_DETONATION with auto_detonated=True
          and anchor in payload (downstream audit)
    - tick() integration: detonation check inside
      `if getattr(self.config, "detonation_enabled", False):` block
      AFTER manual-fire block, BEFORE init-gate. On fire: await execute,
      return early (the tick was dedicated to the harvest).
    - Fold path: buy_cost = _fusd * _taper before _execute_buy. Log

  $0.0000062=BONK). Unworkable.

GROUNDING (R68):
  scrumming_bot.py, grid_bot.py, bot_container.py — all bot.log 
  emissions pass bot_id=self.bot_id to _bus.emit. Confirmed via grep: 
  every emission has the bot_id. So the bug had to be in the 
  renderer, not the emitters.
  
  main_window.py:2478 _on_bot_log:
    message = event.data.get("message", "")
    if message and self._status_log:
        self._status_log.log(message, "info")

IMPLEMENTATION (single file, src/gui/main_window.py):
  Handler now resolves bot_id → bot via BotManager.get_bot, reads 
  ticker from bot.config.target_asset, and constructs prefix 
  '[TICKER/last4] '. Ticker alone would be enough for most cases, but 
  the last-4 suffix disambiguates the (unlikely) case of two bots on 
  the same symbol with different targets — also signals to operator 
  that the id is available if they need to match against logs.
  
  Fallback cascade:
    bot found             → [TICKER/last4]
    bot lookup None       → [last8]
    exception during lookup → [last8] (swallowed, logs never crash)
    no bot_id in event    → no prefix (preserves clean system messages)

WHAT WAS BUILT:

    columns rendered for sub-unit BTC/ETH on small targets.
  • MEM-251 — Structural anchor-ceiling gate at _execute_buy;
    no-dialog, no-exemption cap enforcement.
  • MEM-252 — Target Balance invariant test unified under one file
    (5 AST-level structural checks).
  • MEM-253 — Pre-decision ceiling check at fold-branch entry;
    bot skips buy consideration when already at/above ceiling.
  • MEM-254 — Removed _current_holdings from state persistence.
    Exchange is now authoritative; handshake pulls live on boot.
  • MEM-255 / MEM-256 — bootstrap_exchange_state live-pull on attach
    and on bot register() for restored bots (closes MEM-255 gap).
  • MEM-257 — _execute_buy FAIL-CLOSED: refuses buys unless
    POSITIVELY verified below ceiling. Uses Balance.total (not .free);
    exchange exception → refuse; phantom-zero defense (exchange returns
    0 when local _main_lots show units > 0 → refuse).
  • MEM-258 — tick() delta-zero short-circuit: tick exits IMMEDIATELY
    if |current_value − target_balance| ≤ dust_band. No TA, no signal
    evaluation. BEHAVIORALLY VERIFIED via test that stubs exchange
    whose place_order raises AssertionError on any call (4/4 pass).

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Fail-closed over fail-safe for every buy guard. MEM-251 guard had
    two leak modes (Balance.free missing locked portions, stale-cache
    fallback on exception). MEM-257 policy: unless we POSITIVELY verify
    position is below ceiling, refuse. This accepts false-negatives
    (missed buys) to eliminate false-positives (overbuys past target).
    Operator framing: "EIGHT FUCKING VIOLATIONS ON THIS BRO. ITS A SIMPLE
    FUCKING THRESHOLD THAT MUST BE HELD."

  • Architectural short-circuit at tick() entry over per-path guards.
    MEM-258 moved the at-target check to the very top of tick() rather
    than adding guards at each branch. If position equals target within
    dust_band, NO code path runs — not TA, not signal aggregation, not
    buy/sell branches. Cheaper, more auditable, and structurally impossible
    to accidentally bypass via a new branch added later without ceremony.
    Operator framing: "IF THE GOD DAMN FUCKING CURRENT BALANCE EQUAL
    TARGET BALANCE NO SIGNAL LEAVES THE GOD DAMN PLATFORM."

  • Behavioral verification over source-text assertion for MEM-258.
    The test constructs a real ScrummingBot, stubs an exchange whose
    place_order raises AssertionError on any call, and runs await tick().
    If any buy/sell path fires, AssertionError is raised → test fails.
    Operator framing: "HOW ABOUT YOU VERIFY THE SHIT WORKS INSTEAD."

  • Version bump to 3.15.39 treated as the close-cascade marker.
    Ambient edits to src/trading/phantom_balance.py and volume_guard.py
    landed at 23:50–23:51 PDT 2026-04-23 without a real-time MEM entry;

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Close-time repair of freshness violations is itself rule-laden work.
  An agent with zero SADP context in its window can still be handed the
  freshness error message ("R26 VIOLATION — Chronicle older than HOP")
  and confidently invent a Chronicle entry in a non-canonical format.
  The freshness gate catches mtime drift; it does not catch agent
  orientation drift. This gap was closed by adding sadp/hop_preflight.py

  Born of a narrowly-avoided incident; named for the HOP-protocol gap.

VERSIONS: v3.15.39 -> v3.15.40
================================================================================

Cascade shipped AFTER the Session 26 generational-close CLOSE READY verdict,
driven by operator-reported defects surfaced at close time (Smart Wire drag,
Manual Fire invariant question, "better looking locusts"). Treated as a
follow-on cascade rather than a new session because close already resolved
freshness and the operator's context budget was still healthy.

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  * hop_preflight preventative — sadp/hop_preflight.py (new shared module).
    Emits the R26/R49/R50/R51/R66/R68/R70 core discipline brief as STEP 0
    of both hop_open.py and hop_close.py. Closes the cold-start gap where
    a fresh agent dropped directly into hop_close.py (as happened during
    Session 26 close itself) had no SADP rule text in context yet was
    expected to make rule-laden repair edits when freshness gates fired.

  * Smart Wire drag 1-line fix — src/gui/bot_visualizer.py:908. Wire
    overlay on Bot Swarm viz was created hidden and only shown via
    QTabWidget.currentChanged. Qt does not emit currentChanged for the
    initial tab selection, so the overlay stayed hidden at startup on
    the default tab; clicks fell through to the grid underneath. Fix:
    fire _on_tab_changed(currentIndex) once immediately after connecting
    the signal.

  * Exchange connector defense-in-depth — Balance.absent field;
    ccxt_connector.get_balance() re-checks raw fetch_balance response to
    distinguish "exchange reported zero" from "exchange omitted this
    currency entirely." ScrummingBot handshake hardening: refuses
    initialisation when either read returns absent=True, and when
    handshake reports zero but restored _main_lots say units > 0.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  * Defensive hardening separated from MEM-259 framing. Initial hypothesis
    (re-drawn from the stale Session 25 incident doc) attributed the BONK
    phantom-rebuy to the connector filter + handshake trust-zero path.
    Operator corrected mid-cascade: "BONK issue is old and the same as
    the rebuys troubleshot to VolumeGuard and Phantom Bots." The real
    MEM-259 is the VolumeGuard disable at volume_guard.py:190 (enabled
    hard-coded to return False). The connector + handshake edits are
    still good defense-in-depth — the old fabricated-zero behaviour was
    genuinely ambiguous — but are NOT the canonical BONK remediation.
    Attribution in code comments was reframed accordingly.

  * Half-finished Layer 3 "_initial_entry_completed" latch reverted.
    Dead code that set a never-declared attribute; would have done
    nothing at runtime but implies further work was needed to make the
    latch actually gate initial entry. Rather than finish it without
    operator confirmation, reverted cleanly.

  * hop_preflight designed as non-blocking, always-printed. ~350 tokens
    each invocation; pays the cost every call rather than introducing
    marker files or --confirm-orientation dance. Smooth protocol, no
    friction.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT:

  * Close-time rule-laden repair without orientation is a structural
    protocol gap. hop_close.py would run to completion on a fresh agent
    with zero SADP context. Freshness gate caught mtime drift; it did
    not catch agent orientation drift. hop_preflight.py is the
    structural fix; follow-on rule R71 candidate filed as P3 for
    Session 27.

  * Token Timer metabolism layer was blind for most of this cascade. No
    record() calls during the freshness repair, Smart Wire investigation,
    or initial BONK hypothesis. TT-005 correction_cluster was supposed
    to catch "actively drifting; STOP" — it could not fire because the
    journal didn't see the operator corrections. Reconnected mid-cascade
    after operator flagged "You are losing grounding." Memory entry
    saved to carry this forward.

NEGATIVE RESULTS / WHAT DIDN'T SHIP:

  * P1 Manual Fire gate-bypass audit — clean, no code needed. Audit
    report filed: docs/operator_logs/AUDIT_2026-04-24_manual_fire_gate_bypass.md.
    Bypass invariant already correctly implemented. Operator's "might
    have gated normally before" was most likely the MEM-188 tick-skip
    issue that MEM-242 already fixed.

  * P1b Smart Wire end-to-end — only the drag UI fixed. Engine
    integration (ScrummingBot.set_smart_wire has zero callers,
    _on_wire_created drops pct+target_id, no wire.removed subscriber)
    is architectural and scoped for Session 27 with a PLAN doc first.
    Investigation report filed:
    docs/operator_logs/INCIDENT_2026-04-24_smart_wire_broken_end_to_end.md.
    Do NOT ship the drag fix publicly as "Smart Wire works."

  * Locust refresh P4 — plan filed at sadp/PLAN_LOCUST_REFRESH.md with
    three scopes (A palette only, B pose+animation, C Aseprite sprite
    pipeline). No code shipped this cascade; operator to pick scope and
    Aseprite authoring budget. Grounded in sadp/VISUAL_CRAFT.md
    authorities (Saltsman, DawnBringer, Toby Fox, Medeiros, Williams,
    Hobbs, Ferrari, Entriken).

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  SADP grounding is a three-layer stack, not two. Rules (sadp/SPEC-CORE.md)
  provide the static corpus. Freshness gate (sadp/checklist.py) enforces
  structural drift checks. Token Timers (sadp/token_timer.py) measure
  drift over effort via an event journal. The third layer is the one an
  agent is most tempted to skip — it requires active recording — and its
  absence means the other two can technically be satisfied while the
  agent drifts unseen. The hop_preflight preventative ensures new
  sessions see the rules at STEP 0; the Token Timer discipline ensures
  ongoing sessions watch themselves. Both are now structurally present.

VERSIONS: v3.15.44 → v3.15.45

Two operator-flagged issues: (1) changing Target Balance mid-session

my zip_handoff.py was producing bundles that varied from the operator's
established pattern.

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • ScrummingBot.set_target_balance_live(new_target) — routes live
    operator target changes through a method that updates config +
    _target_balance + _anchor_target_balance in lockstep. Fixes the
    reported bug where Manual Fire and auto fold could not acquire
    the increased position after target-balance raise.
  • bot_live_settings._apply_changes now routes 'target_balance'
    through the new method via a _RUNTIME_ROUTED map. Other fields
    keep the setattr(cfg, ...) path. Future fields that need runtime
    parallels can be added to the map.
  • tests/test_target_balance_live_update.py — 4 tests covering
    lockstep update, bad-value rejection, MEM-253 ceiling with new
    anchor, delta computation with new target. All pass.
  • sadp/zip_handoff.py — scope calibrated to match the operator's
    template bundle (acervator_session25_CLOSE_hop6_v3_16_0.zip):
    scope=ROOT (not ROOT.parent), exclusions match the 490-file
    template, CLOSE filenames carry no descriptor.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Anchor updates with operator-initiated target change: the anchor's
    job is to freeze the set-point against INTERNAL drift (profit-fold
    growth, Smart Wire routing). An EXPLICIT operator raise re-sets
    the set-point — anchor follows. If anchor stayed frozen on
    operator intent, the ceiling guards would refuse every buy that
    moves toward the new target. Operator would see "target raised
    but bot won't buy" — exactly the reported bug.

  • CLOSE filename convention per example: operator's bundles use
    'acervator_session{N}_CLOSE_hop{H}_v{V}.zip' with NO descriptor
    for close-mode; MEM-mode bundles get a descriptor. My earlier
    CLOSE zip included an auto-inferred CHANGELOG descriptor which
    matched a different convention. Aligned to example.

  • Exclusions calibrated by DIFF against the template: original had
    .pytest_cache/ (kept), did NOT have .claude/ or .session26_backups/
    (excluded). Not by theory — by matching what the operator's
    existing bundles actually contain.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT:

  • My initial zip_handoff scope was ROOT.parent — 8 GB bundle. Wrong.
    Operator caught it, linked the canonical template, I aligned.
    Bundle size now ~5 MB matching the pattern.

NEGATIVE RESULTS:

  • Did NOT land P0b Layers 2+3 (projected post-fill ceiling, local
    in-flight tracker). P0b Layer 1 remains the shipped defense.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  When the operator flags drift from a template, the fix is DIFF
  against the template, not theory about what SHOULD be in a bundle.
  Four iterations of zip_handoff happened before I ran a proper
  zipfile-diff between mine and the template. That diff immediately
  showed .pytest_cache/ should be kept and .session26_backups/
  should go — a question settled in one Python one-liner that I had
  been arguing about for a dozen turns.
