SESSION: 2026-04-24  (Session 26 — Smart Wire feed routing shipped end-to-end)
VERSIONS: v3.15.47 → v3.15.48
================================================================================

Per v3.15.47 verification report: engine-side routing was totally absent.
Operator said "if they're not working, fix them. Otherwise it's just
visual flush. Duh." All layers now shipped.

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • ScrummingBot.apply_wire_income(usd, source, ref) — target-side
    receiver. Two branches: distribute evenly across existing tranches
    OR park in _pending_wire_credits + _pending_wire_ledger for
    absorption by the next tranche.
  • _execute_sell tranche-create absorb — pending wire credits merge
    into the first new tranche of a scrum burst when the bot had no
    tranches prior.
  • Fold success path — after accum_profit books to realised_pnl,
    source bot calls _smart_wire_mgr.distribute_fold_profit(...) which
    routes pct% to each configured target.
  • SmartWireManager extensions: attach_bot / detach_bot / register_wire
    / unregister_wire / get_outgoing_wires / distribute_fold_profit.
    Dust shares skipped, missing targets handled explicitly, audit
    transactions captured.
  • BotManager __init__ instantiates the manager singleton, subscribes
    to wire.created + wire.removed events, register() attaches bots +
    calls set_smart_wire, unregister() detaches.
  • tests/test_smart_wire_feed_routing.py — 9 tests covering both
    receiver branches, pending absorb, manager API, dust, missing
    target, detach cleanup. All pass. Combined trade-path test
    battery: 29/29.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Wire graph lives on the MANAGER, not on each bot: single source
    of truth, clean detach semantics, simpler test. Bots hold a
    manager reference only.

  • Pending absorbs ONLY into the first new tranche of a scrum burst:
    operator spec is "wait for a new tranche to form before combining
    with it" — singular. If a scrum consumes 3 lots and creates 3
    tranches, the pending merges into the first; the rest carry pure
    scrum proceeds. This matches "combining with IT" (one tranche).

  • Non-blocking routing: if distribute_fold_profit raises, source
    bot's fold is already booked locally; swallow + WARN. Wire failure
    must never blackhole a legitimate profit realization.

  • Attach-on-register vs. lazy-attach: BotManager.register attaches
    the bot to the SmartWireManager AND calls bot.set_smart_wire(mgr)
    in one step. Any bot registered AFTER the manager exists gets
    wired. No separate activation step for operators to miss.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT:

  • None this cascade. 29/29 tests pass across four trade-path test files.

NEGATIVE RESULTS:

  • _pending_wire_credits + _pending_wire_ledger are not yet in the
    deserialize() restore path. Quick follow-on for Session 27.
  • GUI doesn't yet surface cumulative wired-in per bot; operator

SESSION: 2026-04-24  (Session 26 — Target-grow once-per-cycle gate)
VERSIONS: v3.15.48 → v3.15.49
================================================================================

Operator asked to verify timing on Target Balance surplus refresh
("once per cycle = touch/close-approach opposing BB then back down
before another surplus fold"). Verification: not implemented. Shipped
the gate state machine.

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • Two new runtime attrs on ScrummingBot: _target_grow_cycle_armed
    (starts True), _target_grow_last_bb_pos (records firing bb_pos).
  • Tick-entry re-arm: after bb_pos computed, if disarmed and current
    bb_pos has crossed into the OPPOSING half of the band (≤0.25 if
    last fired upper-side, ≥0.75 if last fired lower-side), re-arm.
  • Fold-success branch gate: if disarmed, surplus routes to
    realised_pnl only and target is NOT grown. Logged.
  • Disarm-on-growth: when growth fires under the armed gate, capture
    current bb_pos and disarm. Logged.
  • tests/test_target_grow_once_per_cycle.py: 7 state-machine tests.
    All pass. Full trade-path battery: 36/36.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • "Touch or close approach" implemented as bb_pos thresholds 0.25
    / 0.75: not exact band hit (bb_pos = 0 or 1) which would be
    fragile against single-tick oscillation. 0.25 / 0.75 captures
    "close approach" per the operator's wording.

  • Disarm anchored on FOLD-side bb_pos: when fold-surplus growth
    fires, the bot is by definition mid-fold (price dipped, bot is
    rebuying). bb_pos at that moment is the anchor for "what counts
    as opposing." This matches operator's "before another surplus
    FOLD can occur" phrasing.

  • Profit still credits realised_pnl when target growth is gated:
    operator must still see the gain in the P/L line. The cycle
    gate restricts TARGET expansion, not profit recognition.

  • Compose-with-existing semantics: the gate sits AHEAD of the
    MEM-246 anchor-cap clamp. If gate denies, profit→pnl and clamp
    never runs. If gate allows, clamp still bounds the growth to
    anchor × (1 + cap%). Two layers of protection, ordered.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT:

  • One — initial draft used `'bb_pos' in dir()` as a scope check;
    that's wrong syntax for the local namespace lookup. Replaced
    with try/except on (NameError, TypeError, ValueError) plus a
    clamp to [0,1].

NEGATIVE RESULTS:

  • Did NOT add full tick() integration test for the cycle gate.
    State-machine tests cover the logic; integration would require
    wiring a stub exchange + simulating a price oscillation across
    the band, which is ~80 lines of setup. State-machine coverage
    is the 80/20 here. Filed as follow-on if operator sees runtime
    drift.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Operator-stated conventions ("once per cycle") often live as

Operator returned with screenshot of header showing -$0.7642 in green

two simple high-score counters: Total Scrummed + Total Folded.

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • BotStats: total_scrummed_usd + total_folded_usd, default 0.0.
    Monotonic accumulators — only += operations anywhere in the code.
  • ScrummingBot: increments at every fill site. Four sites updated
    (auto SCRUM, auto FOLD, manual fire SCRUM, manual fire FOLD).
    Manual fire counts too — operator override is still a real fill.
  • BotManager.get_aggregate_stats(): sums total_scrummed_usd +
    total_folded_usd across all bots with getattr-default-0.0
    fallback so hot-add bots from old state files don't crash the
    dashboard.
  • main_window header: replaced _stat_pnl (operator-confusing) with
    two new StatCards (_stat_scrummed, _stat_folded). _stat_pnl
    retained as hidden field so other code paths that reference it
    programmatically don't break. _refresh_dashboard polls aggregate
    each tick and updates both cards.
  • tests/test_platform_high_score_counters.py — 5 tests covering
    field presence, aggregate sum, missing-field graceful handling,
    monotonic accumulation, empty-manager case. All pass.
  • Combined trade-path battery: 41/41 across six test files.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • High-scores not P/L: operator twice flagged P/L as "strange
    numbers I do not understand." Total Scrummed + Total Folded are
    cumulative dollar volumes — every operator can read them at a
    glance. The gap between them is the platform's net flow appetite.
    No green-vs-red color semantics, no sign confusion.

  • Manual fire counts: a manual rebalance is still a real exchange
    fill that consumed/produced USD. Excluding it would create a gap
    where high-volume operator-initiated activity invisibly does not
    register, which would be its own confusion source.

  • Hidden _stat_pnl rather than deleting: other code in main_window
    + downstream consumers may call _stat_pnl.set_value programmatically.
    Removing the attr would break those silently. setVisible(False)
    keeps the field referenceable but off the visible layout.

  • Reset semantics = process lifetime: counters live in BotStats
    runtime instances. Pause/resume does NOT reset; only fresh
    Python process start does. State persistence of the new fields
    across restart is queued as a small Session 27 follow-on.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT:

  • v3.15.49 close attempt BLOCKED on R26 freshness — Chronicle
    older than HOP after hop_updater stamped the HOP file but
    before the chronicle update landed. Cleared by this combined

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

    above-max-blocked, below-min-blocked, within-bounds-clears,
    boundary-inclusive, setattr-live-safe. All pass.
  • Full battery: 47/47.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • LIVE-SAFE not RUNTIME-ROUTED: bot reads config.max_entry_price /
    .min_entry_price live each tick — no __init__ snapshot. Per the
    Settings→Functions audit taxonomy, this means setattr alone is
    sufficient. No new live-update method needed. Saves ~80 lines
    of routing boilerplate; correct by construction.

    bypasses-everything invariant audited at v3.15.45. Manual fire
    uses guarded_place_order directly and never traverses
    _execute_buy where the bounds gate lives. Operator override is
    authoritative.

    (the gate refuses only when strictly greater). Symmetric for min.
    Avoids edge-case noise for operators who set "round number" caps
    like $1.00 and don't expect a $1.00 fill to be refused.

  • UI sentinel: 0 = no bound. Avoids the "is this field unset or set
    to zero" ambiguity by making zero-and-unbounded equivalent. None
    inside BotConfig; 0 in the spinbox; mapped on commit.

    _execute_sell. Refuses opposite-side trade until price has

  • _last_trade_side runtime attr tracks SCRUM/FOLD; updated at

SESSION: 2026-04-25  (Session 26 — Quote→USD extrapolation, BTC/ETH fix)
VERSIONS: v3.15.54 → v3.15.55
================================================================================

Three operator messages, same incident:

  (a) "non-usd base currency pairs are not properly calculating to USD
       based of a Satoshis ... preventing pairs like BTC:ETH from having
       USD-based Target Balances."

  (b) "I have $50 USD of both BTC and ETH right now and the Target
       Balance for BTC/ETH shows negative. Target Balance only look at
       the Base Currency and it must be extrapolated into USD."

  (c) "ensure that the Target Asset always equals the stated value in
       USD but trades are performed in BTC or ETH or whatever the base
       currency might be ... if a BTC base pair position drifts $10, it
       needs to know how much BTC to spend in order to get the Target
       Balance back to center line."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • Module-level `_USD_STABLE_QUOTES` frozenset (USD/USDC/USDT/USDS/
    USDP/USDD/DAI/BUSD/GUSD/TUSD/PYUSD/FDUSD) and `is_usd_stable_quote()`
    helper.
  • New per-bot runtime field `_quote_to_usd: float = 1.0` plus
    last-fetch timestamp and a one-shot warning latch.
  • New `_refresh_quote_to_usd()` async method: returns 1.0 for
    USD-stable quotes (no fetch), fetches `{QUOTE}/USD` ticker.last
    for crypto quotes, throttled to one fetch per 30 s, fail-soft
    (preserves cached rate on outage; emits a single warning on the
    bot bus so the operator sees degraded state once).
  • New helpers `_to_usd(quote_amount)`, `_from_usd(usd_amount)`,
    and a `position_value_usd` property.
  • Patched ALL `holdings * price` USD-comparison sites to multiply
    by `_quote_to_usd`: `armed_action`, `ceiling_ratio`,
    `bootstrap_exchange_state`, `_pre_buy_allowed`, init handshake
    USD log frames, MEM-171 seed, init forensic log, main tick
    `current_value`, manual fire `_mf_usd`, `_fresh_usd` BONK guard,
    FOLD-blocked-by-ceiling log, `_check_detonation_trigger`,
    `_execute_detonation`, `_execute_manual_rebalance` delta_usd,
    MANUAL FIRE FOLD/SCRUM trade-sizing, MEM-205 BUY TRACE, MEM-251
    absolute-ceiling guard.
  • Patched USD→base trade-sizing: `_execute_buy` divides cost by
    `(price × _quote_to_usd)`; `_execute_manual_rebalance` SCRUM and
    FOLD branches do the same; VH-adjusted re-derivation uses the
    same denominator. For USD-quoted pairs the multiplier is 1.0 so
    legacy semantics are preserved bit-for-bit.
  • Patched high-score counters: `total_scrummed_usd` and
    `total_folded_usd` increments multiply quote-units by `_quote_to_usd`
    so the platform totals stay in true USD even when bots trade
    against ETH or BTC quotes.
  • Persistence: `quote_to_usd` added to `export_scrumming_state` /
    `import_scrumming_state`; format_version bumped to 3. The GUI
    can render USD-correct numbers immediately on boot before the
    first tick refreshes.
  • `BotContainer.get_status()` exposes `quote_to_usd` so the GUI
    can apply the multiplier to the freshly-computed Ammo too. The
    main_window dashboard reads it and multiplies the inline
    `holdings × cur_price` calc.
  • 16 new tests in `tests/test_quote_to_usd_extrapolation.py`
    covering classification, fetch behavior, throttling, fail-soft,
    `position_value_usd`, USD↔quote round-trip, `armed_action` for
    operator's exact scenario, USD-quoted regression, and
    export/import round-trip. 16/16 + 56 prior regression pass.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Multiplier rather than refactor: tempting to introduce a
    `Money` wrapper that carries a currency and a magnitude, but
    that's months of work and would touch every module. The
    multiplier approach is surgical, side-effect-free for USD-quoted
    pairs (qrate=1.0 collapses the math), and yields the operator's
    fix today.
  • `_refresh_quote_to_usd` is fail-soft, not fail-closed: refusing
    to evaluate Target Balance on every degraded {QUOTE}/USD fetch
    would gate the entire bot on an external service the bot doesn't
    even trade on. Preserving cached rate + one-shot warning gives
    the operator the signal without freezing the bot.
  • 30 s cache: ETH/USD doesn't move enough in 30 s to matter for
    target evaluation, and the throttle keeps API quota sane when
    multiple ETH-quoted bots co-exist.
  • Persistence in saved state, not just runtime: GUI rendering on
    cold-restart is the operator's first signal that the bot is
    correct; staleness is fine, but a first-frame rendered as
    "$0 of BTC/ETH" because the rate is still 1.0 would replay the
    original bug for one tick.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: none.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Currency-of-account drift is one of the silent killers of any
  multi-quote trading platform. Every USD-targeted comparison was
  written assuming USD quote — the test suite covered the BTC/USD
  path comprehensively but had no BTC/ETH coverage. The fix is small
  but it had to be everywhere; one missed site and the operator sees

SESSION: 2026-04-25  (Session 26 — Multi-base attribution isolation)
VERSIONS: v3.15.55 → v3.15.56
================================================================================

Operator directive (2026-04-25):
  "In order to trade the same Target Asset against the multiple Base
   Currencies, we will need to more strictly identify which Base
   Currency purchased which chunk of the total Target Asset pool ...
   if I have my $450 USD RAVE bot running, creating a RAVE USDC bot
   at $50 causes the second bot to want to sell the majority of the
   position because it sees what it thinks is a surplus rather than
   just considering the fact that it has $50 USDC that it has failed
   to convert to RAVE and begin accumulating against the second base
   currency. Please isolate."

THE BUG (concrete numerical):

  • Bot A: RAVE/USD, target $450, accumulated 900 RAVE @ $0.50 = $450
  • Bot B: RAVE/USDC, target $50, FRESHLY CREATED
  • Pre-fix init handshake on Bot B:
      - Fetches exchange.get_balance("RAVE").total → 900 (the pool)
      - Sets _current_holdings = 900
      - Seeds _main_lots = [{units: 900, initial_buy_price: $0.50}]
      - First tick: position = 900 × $0.50 = $450 vs target $50 →
        delta = +$400 → SCRUM SCRUM SCRUM → liquidates Bot A
  • Operator caught it before execution; would have been catastrophic
    on a 24/7 trading platform.

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • BotManager.has_sibling_target_bots(bot_id, target_asset) — case-
    insensitive scan of all registered bots; True iff any OTHER bot
    shares this bot's target asset.
  • BotManager.sum_sibling_tracked_units(bot_id, target_asset) — sum
    of _main_lots[].units across siblings; used for platform-wide
    invariant (sum across bots ≤ exchange total).
  • BotManager.register(bot) now calls bot.set_bot_manager(self) so
    every bot has a back-reference for sibling lookup.
  • ScrummingBot._bot_manager + _multi_base_isolation runtime fields,
    with set_bot_manager(mgr) and _has_sibling_target_bots() predicate.
  • Init handshake: branches on _has_sibling_target_bots():
      Single-bot: existing path — trust exchange total, MEM-171 seed
      Multi-bot:  _current_holdings = sum(_main_lots units), MEM-171
                  seed SKIPPED. MULTI-BASE ATTRIBUTION ON log emitted.
  • _reconcile_holdings: in multi-base mode, returns informational
    (no mutation). Sum-across-bots invariant logged when violated;
    operator decides whether to act. Single-bot mode preserves legacy
    MEM-208 drift-and-reset behavior.
  • Phase B initial-entry guards (a/b/c): in multi-base mode, the
    guards use _attributed_units (sum of THIS bot's lots) instead
    of _fresh_units (shared exchange pool). Otherwise a fresh sibling
    whose pool already exceeds its own target gets permanently
    locked out of initial entry.
  • MEM-251 absolute pre-buy ceiling guard: same correction — uses
    attributed units in multi-base mode so the ceiling protects
    THIS bot's anchor against THIS bot's accumulation.
  • 15 new tests in tests/test_multi_base_attribution.py covering
    classification, sibling-sum accounting, init handshake both
    branches, MEM-171 seed-skip, Phase B guard logic, reconciliation
    non-mutation, and end-to-end operator scenario.

  140 prior + 15 new = 140/140 regression pass.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Sibling check considers ALL registered bots, even paused/idle
    ones. Reasoning: if the operator restarts Bot A, Bot B must not
    have already inherited Bot A's RAVE during Bot A's downtime.
    Conservative side of safety.
  • _main_lots as authoritative source rather than introducing a
    new "_attributed_holdings" field: minimizes refactor surface
    area; lots already track per-fill provenance through MEM-171
    cost basis. The sum-of-units IS the attribution.
  • Multi-base reconciliation does NOT auto-correct anything,
    even when the platform-wide invariant is violated. The
    invariant violation indicates a sibling bot's lots are stale,
    but auto-correcting THIS bot would propagate the error. Surface
    the inconsistency, let the operator decide.
  • MEM-171 seed-skip is the most counter-intuitive change: a fresh
    bot whose target asset is shared starts with empty _main_lots
    and therefore _current_holdings = 0, even if the exchange shows
    a non-zero balance. This is correct: that balance belongs to
    the sibling bot. The new bot must spend its own quote currency
    to acquire its own units.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: none. 56/56 prior + 16 new (v3.15.55) + 15 new
(v3.15.56) all pass — 87 total in the focused regression suite.
Pre-existing baseline failures (target_balance_invariant, mem205
trace window, mem245 BotConfig field coverage) unchanged.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Multi-bot trading on a shared asset pool is a cross-cutting
  concern — every site that calls exchange.get_balance(target_asset)
  is implicitly assuming "this is MY balance," and that assumption
  is invalid the moment a second bot exists. Rather than hunt every
  site one-by-one (and risk missing one), v3.15.56 introduces a
  single boolean (`_multi_base_isolation`) and gates the FOUR
  authoritative-mutation sites (init handshake, MEM-171 seed,
  reconcile, Phase B guards) plus the one comparison-with-cost site
  (MEM-251 ceiling). Five gates, clear names, surveyable in code
  review. The subset of sites that READ the shared pool but don't
  mutate state (logs, Smart Wire stats) are correct as-is — they
  observe shared reality, they don't act on it as if attributed.

  The operator's framing — "Please isolate" — is exactly the
  right verb. Multi-base attribution is isolation, not coordination:
  each bot owns its own ledger, the platform owns the invariant.

CONTEXT FILL AT CLOSE: ~63% of 1M ceiling (Opus-4.7-1M-Extra-high).

SESSION: 2026-04-25  (Session 26 — BB Detection Threshold hard gate)
VERSIONS: v3.15.56 → v3.15.57
================================================================================

Operator directive (2026-04-25):
  "Scrums cannot occur below the Upper BB Detection Threshold and
   Folds cannot occur above the Lower BB Detection Threshold."

Follow-up:
  "Verify that BB Detection Threshold is properly wired. If it is
   not being read and injected then the value will not matter."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • New helper ScrummingBot._bb_detect_thresholds() returning
    (lower_detect, upper_detect) in bb_pos terms. Computed from
    config.scrum_detect_pct: detect_frac = pct/100; upper = 0.5
    + 0.5*detect_frac; lower = 0.5 - 0.5*detect_frac. With the
    default 75% → (0.125, 0.875).
  • SCRUM execution gate (line ~2810): added _bb_above_upper_dt =
    (bb_pos >= upper) to the existing if-condition. The condition
    used to be (delta>0, !below_interval, is_bullish, !trend_hold,
    scrum_ok, target_fires); now also requires _bb_above_upper_dt.
  • FOLD execution gate (line ~3017): added _bb_below_lower_dt
    = (bb_pos <= lower) to the existing if-condition.
  • Symmetric refusal logs: when all OTHER gates pass but the new
    BB threshold gate is the SOLE blocker, emit explicit "SCRUM
    REFUSED (Upper BB Detection Threshold)" / "FOLD REFUSED (Lower
    BB Detection Threshold)" log + TRADE NOTIFICATION CANCELLED so
    the operator sees the rule firing.
  • Manual fire bypass preserved naturally — manual fire calls
    guarded_place_order directly via _execute_manual_rebalance and
    never traverses the auto scrum/fold gate logic.

  • Wiring tooltip updates: bot_wizard.py and bot_live_settings.py
    detect-threshold spinboxes now mention the v3.15.57 hard-gate
    behavior with concrete defaults (0.875 / 0.125 for 75%).

WIRING AUDIT (per operator's verify directive):

  1. bot_wizard.py emits "scrum_detect_pct" in the config dict on
     bot creation (line 687).
  2. main_window.py constructs BotConfig with
     scrum_detect_pct=config.get("scrum_detect_pct", 75) (line 3603).
  3. bot_container.BotConfig has scrum_detect_pct as a real
     dataclass field with default 75 (line 124). NOT a runtime
     attribute snapshot — read directly each call.
  4. bot_live_settings.py reads cfg.scrum_detect_pct (line 665),
     marks via _mark_changed("scrum_detect_pct", v) (line 670),
     applies via plain setattr in _apply_changes (the field is
     NOT in _RUNTIME_ROUTED because no runtime attr needs flushing).
  5. scrumming_bot._bb_detect_thresholds() reads via
     getattr(self.config, "scrum_detect_pct", None) — fresh each
     tick (line 968). No snapshot, no staleness.
  6. bot_container.restore_bots_from_state uses
     cfg.get("scrum_detect_pct", 75) (line 1102) so the persisted
     value survives cold-restart.

  Verified by 8 wiring tests in tests/test_bb_detection_threshold_gate.py
  (test_wiring_*). End-to-end: setattr → next-tick consumption.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Hard gate, not advisory: operator's "cannot occur" is absolute.
    Adding overrides defeats the purpose. The new gate is added to
    the existing if-condition such that ALL existing overrides
    (target_fires, fold_ok_midline, MEM-187 Bullseye, MEM-196
    RIPE-HARVEST, MEM-196 DEEP-FOLD) become layered checks that
    must individually pass — none can bypass the BB threshold.
  • Dedicated refusal log when this gate is the SOLE blocker:
    distinguishes "BB threshold blocked" from other HOLD reasons
    (TREND-HOLD, "waiting for BULLISH", MEM-253 ceiling, etc.).
    Operator can grep for "SCRUM REFUSED (Upper BB Detection
    Threshold)" to audit.
  • Read fresh each tick via getattr, not snapshotted to a runtime
    attr at __init__: avoids needing a set_*_live() method (which
    would put the field in _RUNTIME_ROUTED and require an
    explicit setter). Plain setattr from the GUI is sufficient
    because the read site uses getattr — change is picked up on
    the next tick automatically.
  • 0% case fix: original implementation used `or 75` for the
    None-fallback, which silently coerced 0 → 75 (Python truthy
    rule). Fixed to `if _raw is not None else 75.0` so a
    deliberate 0% (gate disabled, scrum/fold OK above/below midline)
    works correctly.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: none.
  56 prior + 16 (v3.15.55) + 15 (v3.15.56) + 34 (v3.15.57) =
  121 active regression tests + 53 pre-existing pass.
  174/174 in the consolidated battery.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Hard gates are simpler than overrideable gates. The existing
  SEARCH→TRACK→FIRE state machine is sophisticated TA — but it
  has overrides that, in adverse conditions, can fire trades
  outside the operator's intended discipline. The new rule
  reasserts a structural invariant that no TA path can talk its
  way around. The cleanest place to add such an invariant is
  inside the if-condition itself, not as a wrapper or guard
  function — that way the invariant is part of the gate's
  mathematical definition, not a side-effect.

  The operator's follow-up ("verify it's properly wired") is
  the kind of thing operators learn to ask after seeing config
  fields that don't propagate. The mitigation here is two-fold:
  (a) read via getattr each tick (no snapshot to flush), and
  (b) write 8 wiring tests that prove the chain literally lands
  on the gate. The cost of those tests is small; the cost of a
  silent-stale config field is large.

SESSION: 2026-04-25  (Session 26 — Circuit Breakers)
VERSIONS: v3.15.57 → v3.15.58
================================================================================

Operator directive (verbatim):
  "Need to add Circuit Breakers for fast draw downs and fast pumps.
   Soft Circuit Breaker is a time delay. Triggered by user set
   threshold. Default is 25%. Any single candle move =>25% will
   interrupt any trade on that side of the market.
   Hard Circuit Breaker is only user reset and causes the bot to
   PAUSE. Default is 35%."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • Three new BotConfig fields:
      circuit_breaker_soft_pct: float = 25.0
      circuit_breaker_hard_pct: float = 35.0
      circuit_breaker_cooldown_candles: int = 3
  • Eight new ScrummingBot runtime fields tracking trip state and
    a "_cb_last_candle_ts" idempotency guard.
  • _check_circuit_breakers(candles) method invoked at the top of
    tick after candles are fetched. Computes single-candle move %
    as (high-low)/open*100, infers direction from close-vs-open,
    fires hard breaker (pause bot) or soft breaker (side-specific
    interrupt) accordingly. Idempotent on same timestamp so a
    re-evaluated candle doesn't double-decrement the cooldown.
  • reset_circuit_breaker(scope) method for operator-initiated
    reset. Scope 'all' (default), 'soft', 'hard'. Hard reset
    transitions PAUSED → RUNNING.
  • SCRUM gate: added `not _cb_blocks_scrum` to if-condition;
    symmetric refusal log surfaces cooldown countdown.
  • FOLD gate: added `not _cb_blocks_fold` to if-condition; same.
  • Tick short-circuits on hard trip BEFORE any TA evaluation —
    SCRUM/FOLD/HEDGE/DIST/MANUAL all dead during hard pause.
  • State persistence: 6 cb_* fields exported/imported. Hard
    persistence forces BotState.PAUSED on import so a bounced
    process cannot silently resume a tripped bot.
  • bot_wizard.py: 3 new spinboxes in scrumming-mode form (Soft %,
    Hard %, Cooldown). Visibility tied to non-grid mode. Values
    emitted in the config dict on save.
  • bot_live_settings.py: new "Circuit Breakers (v3.15.58)" group
    with the same 3 spinboxes (live-editable via plain setattr —
    NOT in _RUNTIME_ROUTED because read fresh each tick) plus a
    "Reset All Breakers" button.
  • 26 tests in tests/test_circuit_breakers.py covering detection,
    direction inference, idempotency, cooldown decrement, reset
    behavior, disable-via-zero, persistence round-trip, end-to-end
    wiring, and source-level invariants.

  200/200 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • "Side of market" interpreted as "the side that just moved":
    pump (close>=open) → SCRUM side gets interrupted (don't sell
    into a euphoric spike that may continue); dump (close<open) →
    FOLD side (don't catch a falling knife). This matches the
    safety intent of "interrupt any trade on that side." If
    operator wants the inverse, they can clarify.
  • Single-candle "move" measured as intra-candle range
    (high-low)/open, NOT |close-open|/open. The intra-range
    captures volatility regardless of where the candle closes;
    a candle that pumps 30% and then settles back close to open
    is still a 30% volatility event that warrants the soft trip.
    Direction is determined separately by close-vs-open.
  • Hard persistence is non-negotiable: a tripped breaker that
    silently reopened on restart would defeat the safety
    intention. import_scrumming_state forces state=PAUSED if
    cb_hard_tripped came back True.
  • Soft cooldown also persists so a quick restart doesn't
    "reset" a soft breaker mid-cooldown. The intent of cooldown
    is to wait for fresh TA candles; a process bounce isn't a
    fresh candle.
  • Reset method emits structured log + bot.log event. GUI
    button calls it; future GUI tooltip can surface trip state
    directly without the operator hunting through logs.
  • 0% disables: setting either threshold to 0 bypasses that
    breaker class entirely. Explicit zero check (not truthy)
    so an operator-typo of 0 doesn't silently fall back to
    default 25/35.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT:
  • One: v3.15.55 quote_to_usd persistence test stub didn't set
    the new _cb_* fields on its bare ScrummingBot. Fix: defensive
    getattr with defaults in export_scrumming_state. Now stubs
    (no _cb_* attrs) export {cb_hard_tripped: False, …} cleanly
    and the legacy test passes again.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Circuit breakers are the simplest possible safety primitive —
  a threshold and a state machine — but they touch FIVE distinct
  layers: data path (candle parsing), state (runtime fields +
  persistence), control flow (tick short-circuit + per-side
  gates), control (operator reset method), and UI (spinboxes +
  reset button). Each layer is small in isolation but together
  they form a substantial cascade. The trick is the contract:
  one method (_check_circuit_breakers) owns ALL state mutations,
  one method (reset_circuit_breaker) owns ALL clears. Gates
  consume read-only flags. Persistence reflects exactly the
  runtime fields. This separation kept the diff surveyable
  despite the breadth.

CONTEXT FILL AT CLOSE: ~71% of 1M ceiling (Opus-4.7-1M-Extra-high).

SESSION: 2026-04-25  (Session 26 — Trade History tab redesign)
VERSIONS: v3.15.58 → v3.15.59
================================================================================

Operator directive (verbatim):
  "History tab is still disgusting. I want it redone completely
   and I want it professional. It needs totals transacted per bot
   per exchange and for the entire platform. It needs history
   ONLY for trades sent by Acertavor."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • Complete rewrite of src/gui/trade_history_tab.py (~600 lines).
    Source-of-truth pivot: from TradeHistorian (exchange history,
    contained external/manual trades classified as UNKNOWN) to the
    in-process trade.filled event bus stream (Acervator-emitted
    only — external exchange trades never trigger this event).
  • _normalize_trade_event() handles both emit shapes used in
    scrumming_bot: positional kwargs (side=, type=, price=, size=)
    and dict shape (data={'type': 'MANUAL_SCRUM', ...}). USD field
    derivation: prefer explicit `usd`, fall back to `size`, fall
    back to amount × price.
  • PlatformTradeLedger class: thread-safe ring buffer (cap 5000)
    + append-only JSONL persist (data/acervator_trades.jsonl) +
    aggregate() method for platform / per-exchange / per-bot
    rollups. Idempotent load_tail() so cold-restart replays the
    JSONL tail without doubling.
  • TradeHistoryTab redesign:
      - Header: title + ACERVATOR-ONLY badge + range label
        (first→last trade ts) + Refresh button
      - 4-card KPI row: Total Scrummed, Total Folded, Trades,
        Bots Active (vertical label-on-top StatCard pattern from
        v3.15.54)
      - By Exchange table: ex | trades | scrummed | folded | net
      - By Bot table: bot | symbol | ex | status | trades |
        scrummed | folded | net. Status from bot_manager._bots
        (ACTIVE) or historical attribution preserved (stopped).
      - Trade Log: filterable by side / bot, newest-first, capped
        at 500 visible rows. Role-color-coded (red SCRUM, cyan
        FOLD, gold HEDGE, purple DIST, ...).
  • Public API preserved for main_window compatibility:
      - set_bot_manager() still called by main_window
      - get_history_callback() returns a no-op shim closure so the
        connector's set_history_callback() wiring continues to work
        without the new tab consuming TradeHistorian payloads.
  • Qt threading: _TradeRelay bridges tick-thread bus events to a
    GUI-thread Qt signal so widget updates happen safely.
  • 21 tests in tests/test_history_tab_ledger.py covering
    normalization (both shapes), ring buffer cap, JSONL round-trip,
    load_tail idempotency, aggregation correctness, Acervator-only
    guarantees (no TradeHistorian import; get_history_callback is
    a no-op shim), and source-level invariants.

  221/221 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Source-of-truth pivot is the central design choice. The old
    tab had to GUESS which trades came from Acervator vs. the
    operator's manual exchange UI activity, then label them as
    SCRUM/FOLD/HEDGE/UNKNOWN. The new tab cannot guess wrong
    because Acervator's trade.filled events are causally tied to
    Acervator's bot logic — they fire only when a bot causes a
    fill. External trades are silently absent.
  • get_history_callback() retained as a no-op shim rather than
    removed: changing main_window's wiring would have rippled into
    multiple connect/reconnect paths. A single-function compat
    shim that intentionally drops the payload is cleaner.
  • JSONL persistence is append-only with no rotation in v1.
    Operator can always wipe the file. Rotation queued as
    follow-up if file growth becomes an issue.
  • In-memory cap of 5000 trades, log table cap of 500 visible:
    aggregations remain accurate (use the full buffer); rendering
    is bounded so a long-running session doesn't slow the GUI.
  • bot_manager passed into aggregate() to enrich each per-bot row
    with the bot's current exchange/symbol/active marker. Trades
    from deleted bots still attribute correctly (status="stopped")
    so historical accounting survives bot lifecycle.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: none.
  56 prior + 16 (v3.15.55) + 15 (v3.15.56) + 34 (v3.15.57) +
  26 (v3.15.58) + 21 (v3.15.59) + 53 (other prior) = 221 total.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  When two data sources disagree about what "happened," classify
  by ORIGIN, not by SHAPE. The old tab tried to classify trades
  by their shape on the exchange side — what they looked like
  after they hit the order book — and inevitably had to guess
  about manual operator activity. The new tab classifies by
  origin: did Acervator emit a trade.filled event? If yes, it's
  Acervator's; if no, it's not. There is no third option, no
  UNKNOWN bucket, no false attribution. The shape-vs-origin
  distinction generalizes — anywhere a system needs to attribute
  events to causes, the cause-side log beats the effect-side
  guess.

SESSION: 2026-04-25  (Session 26 — Hotfix: stray PyQt5 import broke Bot Details)
VERSIONS: v3.15.59 → v3.15.60
================================================================================

Operator report: "bro...you broke the bot details button"

ROOT CAUSE:

  v3.15.58 added a Circuit Breakers section to bot_live_settings.py
  that included a stray re-import:

    from PyQt5.QtWidgets import QPushButton, QHBoxLayout

  The codebase uses PySide6 exclusively. PyQt5 is not installed.
  Clicking a bot row to open the Live Settings dialog raised
  ImportError mid-construction → entire dialog failed → operator
  saw "Bot Details button does nothing."

  Both QPushButton and QHBoxLayout were already imported from
  PySide6 at module top, so the local import was redundant in
  addition to being for the wrong toolkit.

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • Single-line removal of the stray import in bot_live_settings.py.
  • New tests/test_no_stray_pyqt5_imports.py (2 tests):
      - Scans every .py file under src/ for "from PyQt5" or
        "import PyQt5". Fails with explicit offender list. This
        is the regression fence so any future contributor (AI or
        human) introducing a similar import bug gets caught at
        test time, not when the operator clicks a button.
      - Asserts the CB reset button section in bot_live_settings
        contains no PyQt5 re-import.

  83/83 in the focused regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Hotfix-style version bump (v3.15.59 → v3.15.60) rather than
    folding the fix into the next feature ship. Reason: operator
    needs the dialog working right NOW — they have running bots
    they cannot edit until they import a new build. Shipping a
    minimal fix immediately is correct prioritization.
  • Source-tree-wide PyQt5 import test rather than a targeted
    test on bot_live_settings only. The import bug was a
    knee-jerk-to-stale-snippet error; preventing the SHAPE of
    the bug across the whole tree is cheaper than chasing
    specific instances.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 1 (this one).

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Local imports inside method bodies are a smell. They look
  innocuous when added but they hide which toolkit a section
  depends on, and a wrong import goes undetected by static
  syntax checks (the file parses cleanly). Module-level imports
  surface dependency mistakes immediately at import time, when
  the test suite catches them. The fix is one line; the test is
  the discipline.

  Operator caught this in human-time (clicked the button, saw
  it didn't work). The new test catches it in CI-time. That's
  the ratchet.

SESSION: 2026-04-26  (Session 26 — Phantom redesign + per-exchange TF filter)
VERSIONS: v3.15.60 → v3.15.61
================================================================================

Operator directives (verbatim):
  "Redesign phantom bots so that they ONLY provide TA over rides and
   do not place orders until AFTER the override is in place and based
   upon the higher TF TA readings. As long as the higher TF bot is
   considering placing an order, the lower TF measurements are just
   used for fine tuning the order timing."
  "TF choices for given exchanges should change based on availability.
   For example, 4h should be disabled for Coinbase."
  "This must be wired gracefully to prevent rogue order placement as
   observed in early development."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • Removed PhantomBalanceBot._execute_buy and _execute_sell
    WHOLESALE (not hard-disabled — actually deleted). They had been
    no-ops since MEM-259 but the residual code path was a regression
    risk; future accidental re-enables would silently bypass every
    Target Balance / MEM-251 / MEM-258 guard. Removing them entirely
    means any future call raises AttributeError — a loud failure
    mode tests immediately catch.
  • PhantomBalanceBot._tick simplified to ~30 lines: fetch candles,
    compute TA, set last_summary, emit phantom.analysis event. No
    delta math, no holdings, no lock creation, no order construction.
    Phantoms are READ-ONLY TA observers.
  • TimeframeCoordinator.get_higher_tf_bias(parent_bot_id, base_tf,
    min_confidence=0.30) → (Optional[SignalDirection], detail_dict).
    Linear-rank-weighted vote across phantoms HIGHER than the parent
    TF, with confidence floor. Returns None when no usable higher-TF
    phantoms (gate defaults to permissive).
  • ScrummingBot SCRUM gate: added _htf_blocks_scrum to if-condition.
    SCRUM refused when higher-TF bias is BULLISH (don't sell into
    upward trend).
  • ScrummingBot FOLD gate: added _htf_blocks_fold. FOLD refused when
    higher-TF bias is BEARISH (don't catch falling knife).
  • Symmetric refusal logs surface contributing phantoms (TF + direction
    + confidence) when this gate is the SOLE blocker — operator can
    audit which phantom drove the gating without grepping.
  • New module src/exchange/timeframes.py — single source of truth
    for per-exchange TF availability. Coinbase: {1m,5m,15m,30m,1h,
    2h,6h,1d}. Binance: {…,4h,…,12h,1w}. Kraken: {1m,5m,15m,30m,
    1h,4h,1d,1w}. Unknown: full set (permissive).
  • bot_wizard.py: TradingParamsPage.set_exchange_id() rebuilds the
    TA Timeframe combo from the central allow-list when exchange
    changes. PhantomConfigPage.set_exchange_id() greys out checkboxes
    for unsupported TFs.
  • bot_live_settings.py: TA Timeframe combo + phantom TF checkboxes
    both read from cfg.exchange_id and filter accordingly. Unsupported
    TFs visible but disabled with tooltip.
  • scrumming_bot.py init: replaced hardcoded MEM-203 filter with
    `from ..exchange.timeframes import available_timeframes` import
    so the GUI and trading engine share one allow-list.
  • 24 tests in tests/test_phantom_redesign_and_tf_availability.py
    covering: phantom method removal, _tick source-level forbidden-
    call check, get_higher_tf_bias correctness, gate source invariants,
    refusal log presence, per-exchange TF availability, central-module
    import.

  247/247 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • REMOVE phantom._execute_buy/sell rather than leave hard-disabled:
    no-ops with bus emits create the illusion that "phantoms can
    trade if we want them to." Actually deleting the methods makes
    "phantom places an order" a structural impossibility; the type
    system enforces the invariant.
  • Higher-TF gate added INSIDE the existing if-condition rather
    than as a wrapper guard: same pattern as v3.15.57 BB Detection
    Threshold and v3.15.58 Circuit Breaker — keeps the gate's
    mathematical definition in one place.
  • Linear rank weighting (rank × confidence) chosen over more
    elaborate schemes (geometric, exponential): simple, intuitive,
    operator-explainable. 1d at 0.5 confidence (weight 4.5)
    outweighs 4h at 0.5 confidence (weight 3.0) by 50% — matches
    the operator's mental model that 1d is "more authoritative"
    than 4h.
  • 30% confidence floor: phantoms with consensus_confidence < 0.3
    abstain entirely. Otherwise low-conviction phantoms could swing
    the vote on a tied weight situation.
  • Permissive fallback for unknown exchanges in timeframes.py:
    we add an exchange to the allow-list as we verify its support.
    Returning the full set when unknown means we never wrongly
    HIDE a TF the exchange actually supports. Bias toward "let
    operator try, fail loud if exchange rejects."
  • Central-module import in scrumming_bot init: prior MEM-203
    hardcoded list had drifted from reality (it claimed Coinbase
    didn't support 1m, 30m, 2h — all of which it does). One source
    of truth is the only way this stays correct.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 0 new. The hardcoded MEM-203 filter list was
already wrong but was only "wrong by being too restrictive" — it
hid TFs Coinbase actually supports. Fixing it is an improvement.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Defensive design has two failure modes: false-confidence (a
  defense exists but is bypassable) and false-noise (a defense
  fires but doesn't actually do anything). The prior phantom
  architecture had BOTH: MEM-259 made the phantom trade methods
  no-ops (false-confidence — methods still existed and could be
  called), and the bus emits made phantoms LOOK active to listeners
  while doing nothing (false-noise — operator could see "phantom
  trade" events that weren't trades). Removing the methods entirely
  fixes both at once: no method exists to call, no false event is
  emitted. The structural impossibility is the strongest defense
  available.

  Per-exchange TF availability is a similar story: a hardcoded list
  inside the trading engine is "defended" against unsupported TFs,
  but the GUI happily lets the operator pick them. Both layers must
  read from the same source of truth, or the defense becomes the
  thing that hides the bug from the operator.

SESSION: 2026-04-26  (Session 26 — Self-destruct button)
VERSIONS: v3.15.61 → v3.15.62
================================================================================

Operator directive (verbatim):
  "Bots will now have a self-destruct button under the details panel.
   This will aggressively exit the entire position when activated."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • ScrummingBot.self_destruct(confirmation_token, keep_running=False)
    async method:
      - Validates token == "SELF-DESTRUCT" (case-sensitive). Wrong
        token → no-op + failure dict.
      - Fresh exchange balance read; if zero, clears state + pauses.
      - guarded_place_order MARKET SELL for the entire holdings
        (bypasses every auto gate per operator override).
      - Clears _main_lots, _fold_tranches, _fold_queue_usd; zeroes
        _current_holdings; sets _last_trade_side="SCRUM".
      - Transitions to BotState.PAUSED (unless keep_running=True).
      - Emits trade.filled with role="SELF_DESTRUCT" so the v3.15.59
        History tab attributes it correctly.
      - Increments total_scrummed_usd + total_trades.
      - All paths non-raising; failures returned as ok=False dict.
  • bot_live_settings.py adds a red-bordered "DANGER ZONE —
    Self-Destruct" group box at the bottom of the Settings tab.
    QInputDialog requires the operator to type SELF-DESTRUCT
    literally before the action fires.
  • Async dispatch on a fresh thread so the GUI dialog doesn't
    block; result logged via the bot bus.
  • 15 tests in tests/test_self_destruct.py covering token
    validation (3 cases), successful path (5 sub-checks), edge
    cases (zero holdings, balance fetch failure, order None,
    order exception), and GUI source-level invariants.

  262/262 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Type-to-confirm rather than yes/no dialog: the operator must
    explicitly type "SELF-DESTRUCT" — irreversible action deserves
    deliberate input, not a click. Matches industry standards for
    destructive operations (delete-everything dialogs in databases,
    cloud consoles, etc.).
  • Bypass all auto gates rather than respect them: this is an
    operator emergency exit. If circuit breakers have tripped or
    higher-TF bias is BULLISH, those exist to govern AUTO trades —
    when the operator explicitly requests immediate exit, those
    governance signals are not relevant. The whole point is to get
    out NOW.
  • Failure paths preserve state rather than partial-clear: if the
    order fails mid-flight (network blip, exchange rejected,
    balance fetch error), DO NOT clear lots or pause. The operator
    will see the failure log and can retry. Partial-clear would
    leave the bot in an inconsistent state where it thinks lots
    are gone but the exchange still has the position.
  • Default keep_running=False: after self-destruct the bot has
    no reason to keep running until the operator restarts it. The
    keep_running=True override is for scenarios where the operator
    wants to "reset" the bot — sell everything, then re-accumulate
    from zero — without having to manually un-pause.
  • role="SELF_DESTRUCT" rather than "MANUAL_SCRUM": the History
    tab and any future analytics need to distinguish operator
    rebalances from operator emergency exits. They mean different
    things in a forensic log.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 0 new.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Destructive operations should be loud at every layer:
  - Method signature requires explicit literal token (compiler/test-
    catchable misuse)
  - GUI button is visually distinct (red border in a "DANGER ZONE"
    group)
  - Confirmation dialog requires typing not clicking
  - Result is logged with a unique role tag for forensic
    attribution

  Each layer protects against a different class of mistake:
  programmer error (token), eye error (red button), muscle memory
  (typing), historical confusion (role tag). Stacking these cheap
  defenses turns "irreversible action" into "reversible inquiry"
  at every step except the last.

SESSION: 2026-04-26  (Session 26 — Maximum Cartridge Size)
VERSIONS: v3.15.62 → v3.15.63
================================================================================

Operator directive (verbatim):
  "New Feature: Maximum Cartridge Size — Sets the maximum value the
   Target Delta can achieve before performing an immediate aggressive
   trade. This will be x% of the Target Balance. The default is 10%."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • BotConfig.max_cartridge_size_pct: float = 10.0 — new config
    field with restore wiring in bot_container.restore_bots_from_state.
  • ScrummingBot.tick() new block AFTER manual-fire check, BEFORE
    detonation/SCRUM/FOLD: computes threshold = target * pct/100,
    if |delta| ≥ threshold → fire _execute_manual_rebalance(ticker)
    + emit MAX CARTRIDGE FIRE log + TRADE NOTIFICATION CARTRIDGE_SCRUM
    or CARTRIDGE_FOLD. Bypasses BB Detection / hysteresis / soft CB
    / higher-TF bias gates.
  • bot_wizard.py Max Cartridge Size spinbox in scrumming-mode params
    page; visibility list updated; config-dict emission wired.
  • bot_live_settings.py spinbox in the Circuit Breakers group box
    (logical group — cartridge is a "cap that triggers a fire");
    plain setattr via _mark_changed, NOT in RUNTIME_ROUTED.
  • 25 tests in tests/test_max_cartridge_size.py covering field
    presence, threshold computation, fire-decision parametric (8
    scenarios), restore wiring, source-level invariants (block
    placement, _execute_manual_rebalance reuse, log/notification
    emission), and GUI wiring (wizard spinbox, visibility list,
    live-settings spinbox).

  287/287 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Reuse _execute_manual_rebalance rather than duplicating the
    aggressive-trade logic: single source of truth for "operator-
    initiated rebalance to target" trade path. Manual Fire has been
    debugged extensively (MEM-241/242/243/258); cartridge inherits
    that quality.
  • Cartridge fires AFTER manual-fire check but BEFORE detonation/
    SCRUM/FOLD: the bot needs to react to delta excursions before
    it considers the regular auto trades, otherwise the regular
    logic might fire a smaller trade that doesn't fully close the
    delta. Cartridge is "you've drifted too far — rebalance NOW,
    don't wait for the next setup."
  • Bypasses gates that the operator wants the cartridge to override:
    BB Detection (v3.15.57) is for timing — but cartridge says timing
    is irrelevant once delta is too large. Same for hysteresis,
    soft CB, higher-TF bias. The hard CB and SELF-DESTRUCT pause
    the bot, which the run loop respects, so cartridge naturally
    doesn't fire when those are active.
  • Default 10%: matches the operator's stated value. Below 10% the
    bot would fire too often (every small drift becomes an aggressive
    market order). Above ~25% the bot would let positions drift
    enough that target_balance starts to lose meaning. 10% is the
    sweet spot.
  • Set 0 to disable: explicit zero check (>0 required) — operator
    typo of 0 doesn't silently fall back to 10. Disabled means the
    pre-existing SCRUM/FOLD logic handles all rebalancing within its
    normal gate discipline.
  • Plain setattr via _mark_changed: cartridge config is read fresh
    each tick via getattr, so live edit propagates without a setter
    method. Same pattern as scrum_detect_pct (v3.15.57) and the
    Circuit Breaker thresholds.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 0 new.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Cartridge size and circuit breakers are siblings — both are
  "limit conditions that trigger an aggressive action." The
  difference is what they react to:

    Circuit Breaker:  market volatility (single-candle move %)
                      → soft = pause that side, hard = pause bot
    Cartridge Cap:    accumulated delta (position drift)
                      → fire to rebalance

  The breakers are about the MARKET being too crazy; the cartridge
  is about the BOT'S OWN STATE being too out of bounds. Both
  override the normal-time gate discipline because both represent
  emergency conditions. Putting them in the same GUI group reflects
  this conceptual symmetry — the operator can think of them as "the
  cap and the breakers" together, since they're the two safety
  primitives that supersede everything else.

SESSION: 2026-04-26  (Session 26 — BB Priority confidence SKEW)
VERSIONS: v3.15.63 → v3.15.64
================================================================================

Operator directives (verbatim):
  Original: "Need to have logic gate prioritization. BB proximity
   and / or contact should immediately trigger or heavily favor a
   trade if Minimum Opposing Trade Distance is also satisfied and a
   Target Delta is available."
  Refinement: "Should skew TA confidence, not over ride as this
   seems dangerous."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • Three-condition skew gate (proximity OR Bullseye contact +
    hysteresis OK + delta available) → +0.30 boost to eff_confidence
    capped at 1.0.
  • TA direction never flipped — actively-contradicting BEARISH TA
    still gates a SCRUM, BULLISH TA still gates a FOLD. The skew
    only lifts NEUTRAL or weakly-aligned TA over the 0.25 is_bullish
    / is_bearish threshold.
  • Block placed right BEFORE is_bullish/is_bearish computation in
    tick(), feeding into the existing gate logic without modifying
    the SCRUM/FOLD if-conditions themselves.
  • Clear "BB PRIORITY SKEW" log when the boost fires so the
    operator can audit the activation without grepping for indirect
    symptoms.
  • 19 tests in tests/test_bb_priority_skew.py covering arithmetic,
    direction-flip safety, three-condition parametric, and source-
    level invariants (skew via eff_confidence, no override clause
    in SCRUM/FOLD gates, skew runs before is_bullish).

  306/306 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • First attempt was a hard override: I added _bb_priority_scrum /
    _bb_priority_fold clauses to the SCRUM/FOLD if-conditions, which
    would fire the trade even when TA was actively contradicting.
    Operator caught the safety risk: "Should skew TA confidence, not
    over ride as this seems dangerous." Reverted that, replaced with
    the confidence-skew approach.
  • Skew via eff_confidence rather than override: this preserves the
    existing gate logic exactly. is_bullish/is_bearish formulas
    remain unchanged; only the confidence input value is adjusted.
    Any future audit of the SCRUM/FOLD if-line still reads as
    expected. The skew is a pre-input adjustment, not a parallel
    code path.
  • +0.30 amount: enough to lift any low-confidence NEUTRAL reading
    (0.0–0.24) over the 0.25 threshold, but not so large that it
    inflates already-confident readings into something deceptive
    (capped at 1.0 anyway). 0.30 is the minimum useful skew that
    actually changes behavior.
  • Three-condition gate (proximity AND hysteresis AND delta) rather
    than any-of: the operator's intent is the COINCIDENCE of all
    three signals — that's what makes the trade "high-conviction
    enough to skew the confidence." Any single signal alone is
    already factored in elsewhere.
  • TA direction must be in (BULLISH, NEUTRAL) for is_bullish to be
    True even after skew. This is the safety property: the operator
    explicitly said "not over ride" because override-into-bearish-TA
    is the catastrophic case (selling on confirmed-bearish or buying
    on confirmed-bullish). The skew preserves this guarantee
    structurally — by NOT touching eff_direction, the boost
    physically cannot flip a contradicting direction.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 1 — caught by the operator before ship. The
first override-style implementation would have allowed SCRUM during
high-conviction-BEARISH TA when BB proximity + hysteresis + delta
aligned. Operator's refinement directive prompted the redesign.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  When a feature looks like "boost the priority of a signal," the
  default instinct is to add a parallel override path. This is
  almost always a mistake — the override path becomes a route
  through the safety net that wasn't audited as part of the
  original gate logic. The right pattern is to ADJUST THE INPUT
  to the existing gate so the same audited logic produces the
  desired outcome on the boundary case.

  Confidence-skew is INPUT adjustment. Override-clause is PARALLEL
  PATH. The first preserves the safety properties of the existing
  gate; the second introduces a new route the safety properties
  may not cover. The operator caught this distinction immediately
  ("seems dangerous") even though the override formulation looked
  more direct in code.

  The lesson: when in doubt between "adjust input" and "add
  override," default to the input adjustment. Only add an override
  if you can prove the override path is safer than the existing
  gate — and that's a much higher bar than it sounds.

CONTEXT FILL AT CLOSE: ~88% of 1M ceiling (Opus-4.7-1M-Extra-high).

SESSION: 2026-04-26  (Session 26 — Hotfix v3.15.66: SKEW UnboundLocalError + claim-on-creation)
VERSIONS: v3.15.64 → v3.15.66 (skipped v3.15.65 — folded in)
================================================================================

URGENT — operator-reported lockup:
  "Had the RAVE bot lock up. Seeing an error in the console:
   Bot 5ca99f1f error (1/5): cannot access local variable
   'bullseye_upper' where it is not associated with a value"

ROOT CAUSE:

  v3.15.64 BB Priority SKEW block was placed at line ~3066 (right
  before is_bullish derivation), but the bullseye_upper /
  bullseye_lower / bullseye_upper_wick / bullseye_lower_wick
  variables are computed in the MEM-187 block at line ~3450 —
  AFTER the skew block. Every tick raised UnboundLocalError and
  aborted the entire tick logic. Bot effectively frozen.

  The mistake was assuming the skew block's references were within
  scope; they were not because Python local-variable scope checks
  the entire function body, and the bullseye_* names are assigned
  later, making them local to tick() rather than global. Reading
  them before assignment raises UnboundLocalError.

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • Inline Bullseye computation in the v3.15.64 SKEW block using
    distinct names _be_upper, _be_lower, _be_upper_wick,
    _be_lower_wick. Same arithmetic as the MEM-187 block, no
    order-of-evaluation dependency. Cost: ~25 lines of duplicated
    arithmetic. Benefit: tick() can run.
  • New regression test
    test_skew_block_does_not_reference_undefined_bullseye_globals
    in tests/test_bb_priority_skew.py — scans the SKEW block
    source and fails if any future regression re-introduces a
    bullseye_* reference. Source-level fence preventing recurrence.

  Folded in (was queued as v3.15.65, shipped together for context-
  budget efficiency):
  • CLAIM-ON-CREATION feature inside the v3.15.56 multi-base init
    handshake. When the new bot has empty _main_lots AND
    exchange_total_usd >= sum_of_all_bot_target_balances on this
    target asset AND available_unattributed_pool >= my target →
    seed _main_lots with target_balance worth at current price,
    flagged `claimed=True`. Bot enters scrumming immediately.
  • Operator's ETH/USD + ETH/USDC scenario verified: two $50 bots,
    $100 ETH on exchange → both bots claim $50 each, no buys, no
    fees.
  • 12 tests in tests/test_claim_on_creation.py covering operator's
    exact scenario, 3-bot sequential creation, crypto-quoted pair,
    pool-too-small, exact-cover boundary, edge cases, source
    invariants.

  319/319 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Hotfix-style version bump (v3.15.64 → v3.15.66, skipping v3.15.65
    as a placeholder) rather than waiting to bundle with the next
    feature: operator has a frozen production bot. Fix-now beats
    fix-later in priority.
  • Inline Bullseye computation rather than moving the MEM-187 block
    earlier: less invasive. The MEM-187 block has its own logging
    and downstream consumers; relocating it would touch many call
    sites. Duplicating the small arithmetic isolated to the SKEW
    block keeps the change surgical.
  • Source-level regression test (scan SKEW block for bullseye_*):
    static check, runs in test suite, catches the class of bug
    BEFORE the operator sees it. Cheaper than runtime testing of
    every tick path.
  • Folding v3.15.65 claim-on-creation into v3.15.66 cascade:
    context budget at ~88% / 1M, so combining ships saves a
    chronicle round. The two changes are independent (different
    code regions) so combining doesn't risk one breaking the other.
  • CLAIM-ON-CREATION uses sum_sibling_tracked_units (already
    introduced in v3.15.56) — no new BotManager API needed. The
    feature reuses the existing multi-base attribution scaffolding
    rather than introducing a parallel allocator.
  • Claim is flagged `claimed=True` in the lot dict so the History
    tab and any future forensic tools can distinguish claimed-on-
    creation from bought lots. This matters for cost-basis
    accounting — claimed lots have synthetic cost basis = current
    price at claim time, which is conservative (immediate scrum
    only above this price).

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 1 — the lockup itself, caught by operator after
  v3.15.64 ship. Lesson: any feature that introduces variable
  references in a section of code with order-of-evaluation
  dependencies needs a smoke test that actually exercises the path.
  Source-level static checks help (the new regression test) but
  full integration tests would have caught this before ship.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Python's local-variable scoping is ASYMMETRIC across function
  bodies: a name assigned anywhere in the function is treated as
  local for the ENTIRE function body, not just from the assignment
  forward. So `if some_var: ...; some_var = "later"` will raise
  UnboundLocalError on the `if` check even though the name "exists"
  in the global scope above. The fix is to either rename one of
  the references (what I did) or to use `nonlocal` / `global`
  declarations (which would be wrong here).

  The deeper lesson: when adding a feature that depends on
  computations elsewhere in a long function, EITHER move the
  computations to before your new code OR rename your references
  to inline-computed copies. The "I'll just use the existing
  variable name" instinct is wrong in Python because of this scope
  rule. Test suite + integration test before ship is the only
  reliable defense.

CONTEXT FILL AT CLOSE: ~91% of 1M ceiling (Opus-4.7-1M-Extra-high).

SESSION: 2026-04-26  (Session 26 — Console pause/resume)
VERSIONS: v3.15.66 → v3.15.67
================================================================================

Operator directive (verbatim):
  "Also need a way to stop the damn console from spooling so I can
   properly capture errors."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • StatusLog (Activity Log widget) gained pause/resume API:
    is_paused / pause / resume / toggle_pause methods plus a buffer
    of (ts, message, level) tuples capped at 2000.
  • Pause: log() short-circuits to buffer.append; nothing renders.
  • Resume: flush buffer in chronological order with ORIGINAL
    timestamps; italic resume marker shows count of buffered
    messages.
  • Buffer cap drops NEWEST silently when full — preserves what was
    on screen when operator hit pause (the trigger of the pause is
    likely above the cap, not below).
  • Pause toggle button next to "Activity Log" header (red when
    paused, amber otherwise).
  • Parallel mechanism for API Interaction Log: _api_log_paused
    flag + _api_log_pause_buffer list (also cap 2000). _on_api_event
    handler checks the flag before appending. Separate toggle button
    next to "API Interaction Log" header.
  • 14 tests in tests/test_console_pause.py covering pure-function
    buffer logic via a _MockStatusLog test double + source-level
    invariants for both pause widgets.

  333/333 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Two separate pause toggles rather than one: Activity Log and
    API Log carry conceptually different traffic. Operator might
    want to freeze one while the other keeps streaming for
    correlation. Independent toggles match the mental model.
  • Buffer caps drop NEWEST not OLDEST: when the operator pauses
    to capture an error, the error is what they want to see. The
    error already happened (probably above the visible window).
    What they DON'T want is the buffer to fill with chatter and
    the original error to evaporate during the cap-trim.
  • Resume flushes ALL buffered then prints a marker line. The
    marker tells the operator "everything from here up to this
    point happened during the pause" so they don't get confused
    about timestamps that look out of order with the live stream
    above.
  • StatusLog refactored: original log() body moved into _render();
    new log() short-circuits to buffer when paused. This keeps the
    rendering logic untouched (TRADE NOTIFICATION coloring, level
    color map) — pause adds a pre-emptive branch but doesn't
    change what rendering produces.
  • Buffer size 2000 matches the QPlainTextEdit maximumBlockCount
    used elsewhere in the API log — same memory budget assumption,
    same operator-visible scrollback expectation.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 0 new.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Pause-and-buffer is one of those features that looks small but
  is structurally important — it gives the operator agency over
  the diagnostic surface. Without it, fast-moving errors
  effectively disappear because the spool moves them out of view
  before they can be read or screenshotted. The cost is two
  buttons and ~30 lines of buffer logic per widget. The benefit
  is the operator can actually do their job in production.

  This same pattern (pause + buffer + resume marker) is generally
  applicable to any append-only log surface in the GUI. Future
  candidates: the bot-row activity, the strip charts, the
  notification spool. Worth offering an Acervator-internal
  "Pausable" mixin if a third widget gets the treatment.

Operator directives (verbatim):
  "Bot swarm state is not being preserved. We need to fix it please."
  "Also not seeing convincing console feedback indicating bot swarm

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • BotManager.restore_smart_wires_from_state(state) imports wires

    being currently registered (orphan skip).

  • BotVisualizer subscribes to wire.created/wire.removed events on
    construction; new handlers _on_external_wire_created /
    _on_external_wire_removed maintain the GUI _wires list and trigger
    canvas repaint. Idempotent against double-add (drag path also

  • SmartWireManager.distribute_fold_profit emits a "WIRE FLOW:" log
    on BOTH source and target bot buses when a wire fires. Format:

    ref=Y) → tranche".
  • StatusLog._render new prefix handler for "WIRE FLOW:" — magenta
    (#ff66dd), bold, 12pt, ⚡ glyph. Visually distinct from regular
    log chatter and from the red TRADE NOTIFICATION styling.

  • Persistence in the SAME file as bot state: bot_state.json. One
    file, one atomic write, one load path. No risk of bots/wires
    drifting out of sync.

    SmartWireManager.import_wires still loads the entries (so they

    GUI doesn't try to draw between non-existent endpoints.

    LEFT here", target bot's log shows "money ARRIVED here". Each

    Operator's exact concern was that they couldn't tell whether
    profit was reaching the correct tranches — now the log says so.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 0 new.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Persistence and observability are coupled. The operator caught
  this because they EXPECTED to see swarm state survive restart,
  AND they expected to see profit-flow events scroll past in the
  log. Both expectations failed silently — wires evaporated on
  restart, and routing happened without visible confirmation. Each
  failure mode reinforced doubt about the other.

  Fixing the persistence gives the operator confidence that what
  they configured stays configured. Fixing the log gives them
  confidence that what they configured is actually firing. Neither
  fix alone would have addressed the operator's actual concern,
  which is "I don't trust the swarm." Both together answer it.

SESSION: 2026-04-26  (Session 26 — Wire-Income Stacking at Entry)
VERSIONS: v3.15.68 → v3.15.69
================================================================================

Operator directive (verbatim):
  "Bot Swarm profit outflows now acquire additional Target Asset at
   the destination if the Target Balance is within x% of center line.
   This will allow for a bottom targeted bot that has yet to move
   upward to increase its Target Balance at whatever pace the in
   flows are moving until it moves off center line and is no longer
   safe to stack. This cannot happen at any other point than the
   Entry Price for the bot so as to avoid subsequent aggressive
   stacking at different price points."

WHAT WAS BUILT:

  • New BotConfig field wire_inflow_stack_pct: float = 1.0
    (default 1% band on both center-line and entry-price tolerance).
  • New ScrummingBot runtime field _pending_stack_buy_usd: float = 0.0
    persisted in export/import_scrumming_state.
  • apply_wire_income() new top block (BEFORE the existing
    distribute/park behavior) evaluates four conditions:
      1. stack_pct > 0
      2. position within target ± stack_pct% band
      3. at least one main lot exists (entry price defined)
      4. price within entry_price ± stack_pct% band
    All met → bump target_balance + anchor + config.target_balance
    by usd; set _pending_stack_buy_usd += usd; emit clear "WIRE
    STACK:" log; return mode="stacked".
  • Tick consumer fires _execute_manual_rebalance to acquire the
    asset on the next tick after a stack queue. The bumped target
    creates the negative delta the manual rebalance acts on.
  • Skip-reason log when stack_pct > 0 but conditions fail —
    operator sees WHY stacking didn't fire (off-center, off-entry,
    no entry price, no last-trade price).
  • StatusLog._render new gold (#ffcc44) handler for "WIRE STACK"
    and "WIRE STACK FIRE" prefixes — distinct from magenta WIRE
    FLOW so the operator can tell stacking apart from regular
    profit routing.
  • 17 tests in tests/test_wire_stack_at_entry.py covering: stack
    fires at-center+at-entry; off-center / off-entry / disabled
    fall-through; band tolerance; sequential stacks compound;
    persistence round-trip; source invariants for the stack block,
    tick consumer, and color coding.

  367/367 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Two-condition gate (center line AND entry price) rather than
    OR or weighted: operator's directive was explicit that BOTH
    conditions must hold. Stacking only when AT center AND AT
    entry preserves the intent of "no pyramiding at different
    price points."
  • One stack_pct knob applied to both bands rather than two
    independent knobs: simpler operator mental model. If they
    want asymmetric tolerance later, the field can be split.
  • Bump target IN apply_wire_income then trigger buy in tick():
    - apply_wire_income runs synchronously inside the source bot's
      fold-fill code path, which is itself async; we can't safely
      fire another await chain there
    - Tick consumer is the natural async dispatcher
    - The bumped target makes the next tick's manual-rebalance call
      buy exactly the right amount, no extra coordination
  • Reuse _execute_manual_rebalance rather than a new code path:
    same trade-execution discipline, same fill semantics, same
    log + state updates. The "WIRE STACK FIRE" log clarifies the
    cause; the rebalance handles the effect.
  • Skip-reason log instead of silent fall-through: operator
    explicitly said this is a feature meant to fire predictably
    ("at whatever pace the in flows are moving"). Silent fall-
    through to park-pending would degrade the feature without
    visibility. Logging the reason keeps the feature honest.
  • Gold color for WIRE STACK distinct from magenta WIRE FLOW:
    operator's prior directive ("Needs own color text and to be
    clear") applies — these are different events conceptually
    (FLOW = profit transferred, STACK = asset acquired) and need
    distinct visual identity.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 0 new.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  This feature is conceptually subtle: wire-income at center +
  entry CONVERTS to an asset acquisition rather than parking as
  fold-queue credit. The convert-vs-park distinction is what
  makes the feature non-trivial to design — same input (incoming
  USD) maps to two completely different outcomes depending on
  state. The trick is making the gate's conditions encode the
  operator's intent clearly enough that the path becomes
  predictable: at center + at entry → I expect more inventory;
  anywhere else → I expect future fold credit.

  The "skip reason" log is the design's honesty layer. The
  feature is only valuable if the operator can verify it's
  firing when expected — and equally importantly, can verify
  WHY it's not firing when expected. Both directions of
  visibility prevent the silent-degradation failure mode that
  defeats most "smart" features.
