SESSION: 2026-04-26  (Session 26 — armed_action requires init handshake)
VERSIONS: v3.15.69 → v3.15.72  (three-iteration fix; intermediate
                               v3.15.70/v3.15.71 ships did not solve
                               the operator's bug; v3.15.72 is the
                               actual root-cause fix)
================================================================================

Operator escalation chain:
  v3.15.70 ship: "That did not fix it. Dig deeper."
                "Both latched green as soon as I launched .70.
                 And started them back up."
                "State consideration data for bots should be live
                 pulled. Recovery for them is not saving stale
                 prices, its doing an auto API refresh on Start."
                "Other than their settings of course..."
                "Do not leave dangling fixes that did nothing or
                 produced slop code. Keep it clean."
  v3.15.71 ship: "DUDE. Fail no.2."
                 "ROOT FUCKING CAUSE NOW"
                 "Stop ending your process at the first indicator.
                  It could be at the end of a chain of events."

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE (only fully understood at v3.15.72):

  Chain of events:
  1. Bot restored from saved state — _main_lots, target_balance
     etc. restored.
  2. MEM-254 deliberately does NOT restore _current_holdings from
     save state ("exchange is authoritative; the MEM-226 handshake
     repopulates on boot"). So between restore and the first tick,
     _current_holdings = 0 (the __init__ default).
  3. bootstrap_exchange_state fires in a background thread (per
     MEM-256) and sets stats.current_price + stats.position_value
     from the live ticker + balance call.
  4. The bot now has fresh price but pre-init zero holdings.
  5. v3.15.71's armed_action evaluated 0 × fresh_price × qrate
     = $0 → delta = -target → returned 'fold' → button GREEN at
     launch even though the bot's real holdings aren't yet known.
  6. The first tick eventually fires the init handshake → sets
     _current_holdings → armed_action then evaluates correctly.
     But the operator already saw the wrong button.

  The first two ships (v3.15.70 prefer-fresh-with-fallback,
  v3.15.71 fresh-only-no-fallback) addressed the PRICE staleness
  but not the HOLDINGS staleness. The actual chain has BOTH issues
  and only fixing both gives the operator the right state at launch.

WHAT WAS BUILT (v3.15.72 final):

  • armed_action now requires self._initialised = True. The init
    handshake (which validates exchange holdings and either restores
    _current_holdings from _h2 or sums _main_lots in multi-base
    mode) is the moment the bot KNOWS its real position. Before
    that, returning None is correct.
  • Comment in armed_action documents the full operator-reported
    chain so future maintainers understand why this gate exists.
  • Test stubs (test_mem241_manual_fire_rebalance.py,
    test_quote_to_usd_extrapolation.py, test_armed_action_uses_
    fresh_price.py) updated to set _initialised=True (default
    True in the v3.15.71 stub helper).
  • New regression test
    test_armed_action_returns_none_when_not_initialised — locks in
    the v3.15.72 contract: pre-handshake state returns None even
    if fresh price is available.

  376/376 in the consolidated regression battery.

KEY DECISIONS & RATIONALE:

  • Three conditions must hold for armed_action to evaluate: (1)
    target balance is set, (2) handshake completed (_initialised),
    (3) fresh ticker price available. Missing any → None. Operator's
    "live pulled" directive applies to ALL inputs of the decision,
    not just one.
  • Don't auto-promote bootstrap's holdings into _initialised. The
    handshake has additional validations (two-read MEM-226 protocol,
    absent-sentinel check, lots cross-check, multi-base attribution
    branch). Those are all the work that `_initialised` truly
    represents. Treating bootstrap's read as "good enough" would
    paper over those checks.
  • Three-ship fix rather than batched: each iteration was needed
    to surface the next layer of the chain. The operator's
    "ROOT FUCKING CAUSE" directive forced the right level of
    diligence — looking past the first observed divergence to the
    deeper sequence.

REGRESSIONS CAUGHT: 2 (my own — v3.15.70 wrong fallback, v3.15.71
incomplete fix), both caught by the operator within minutes of
each ship. The lesson is in the operator's directive: "Stop ending
your process at the first indicator. It could be at the end of a
chain of events." Stale-state bugs at startup typically have
multiple components (price, holdings, target, sometimes lots).
Fixing one component while leaving others stale produces a
different but still-wrong observable state.

NEGATIVE RESULTS: none.

KEY INSIGHT (session close):

  Launch-time correctness has multiple input axes:
    - Price (live ticker)
    - Holdings (live balance + multi-base attribution)
    - Target (operator-set, persisted)
    - Lots (persisted, restored)
  All must be live-pulled / live-restored before any decision
  surface (Fire button, Ammo, FOLD/SCRUM gates) can produce truth.
  ANY one being stale means the decision surface is fabricating.

  The right pattern: at startup, decision surfaces wait for ALL
  their inputs to reach a known-good state. The waiting period is
  brief (≤1s for bootstrap; first tick at scrum_read_rate). During
  the wait, the surface shows "unknown" — not a guess.

  This generalizes beyond armed_action. The pattern applies to:
  Ammo column (don't show stale max(stats_pv, fresh_pv); show
  pending until all inputs live), bot row Trades count (already
  correct since stats are persisted), bot row state badge (already
  correct since state is persisted). Audit pass for "does this
  surface fabricate during launch" is a follow-up.

ROOT MOTIVATION: The Confidence Index is the engine's primary trade-gate
input. Until this ship, it lived only in source code (ta_engine.py
VotingEngine + scrumming_bot.py eff_confidence cascade). The product
manual described individual indicators (§6 Signal Inventory) but never
documented how their votes aggregate into the single number that gates
SCRUM/FOLD decisions. Operator-facing documentation needed the equation.

WHAT WAS BUILT (v3.15.73):

  New section §6.5 The Confidence Index in build_product_manual.py,
  inserted between §6 (Signal Inventory) and §7 (Provenance Fold Queue).
  Six sub-sections:

  6.5.1 Per-indicator weighted score:
        weighted_score = direction × confidence × weight

  6.5.2 Default indicator weights (table from DEFAULT_WEIGHTS):
        macd 1.20, ichimoku 1.10, bollinger_bands/stochastic_rsi/
        slingshot/adx 1.00, vortex 0.90, volume 0.80

  6.5.3 Single-timeframe consensus:
        consensus_confidence = min(1.0, |bull_score − bear_score|
                                        / total_weight)
        with consensus_direction from sign of net.

  6.5.4 Multi-timeframe aggregation:
        Indicator weight × TF weight before re-aggregation.
        Ladder: 1m=0.30, 5m=0.50, 15m=0.70, 30m=0.85, 1h=1.00,
                2h=1.10, 4h=1.30, 6h=1.35, 12h=1.40, 1d=1.50, 1w=1.60.

  6.5.5 Effective confidence:
        eff_confidence = consensus_confidence
                       + position_boost          (±0.03 to ±0.20)
                       + bb_confidence_boost     (+0.15 to +0.35)
                       + bb_priority_skew        (+0.30, never flips
                                                  direction)

  6.5.6 Trade gate threshold:
        is_bullish/is_bearish at eff_confidence ≥ 0.25.
        Full gate stack: direction → effective confidence → BB Detect
        Threshold → Circuit Breaker → Higher-TF Bias → trade.

SESSION: 2026-04-26 (Session 26 — continuation)
VERSIONS: v3.15.74
TITLE: Smart Wire visibility — silent dust-skip surfaced
================================================================================

OPERATOR DIRECTIVE: "Still not seeing bot smart distributions in the
console. Perform root cause. Need it working and need to also make
sure folds are compounding properly."

CONTEXT: Operator sent this mid-flight while the v3.15.73 manual
ship was finishing. The smart wire WIRE FLOW logs from v3.15.68 were
expected to provide visibility into source→target profit routing but
the operator was seeing nothing in the console even though folds were
firing.

ROOT CAUSE (R68 cold-read):

  SmartWireManager.distribute_fold_profit silently early-skipped any
  per-wire share below `_min_wire` (default $1.00). The skip was
  captured in the returned results list but no `bot.log` event was
  emitted. In flat markets, fold profits are small ($0.50–$3.00); with
  a typical 30% wire pct, shares routinely fell below the $1.00 floor
  and the operator saw nothing. The fold path itself was working
  correctly — the visibility layer was the problem.

  This was a textbook "stop ending your process at the first indicator"
  case (per Session 26 v3.15.72 lesson). The first visible symptom
  ("no WIRE FLOW logs") looked like the WIRE FLOW emission was broken,
  but tracing the full chain — fold → distribute_fold_profit →
  per-wire share computation → dust filter → skip-without-log — found
  the actual point of silent loss.

SECONDARY OBSERVATIONS:

  • Folds ARE compounding mathematically (verified by cold-read of
    scrumming_bot.py:4330–4356). Each successful fold grows source
    _target_balance by accum_profit, books accum_profit to
    realised_pnl, and routes pct% to target bots whose
    _fold_queue_usd grows by their share. Future folds operate on
    the new larger state — that is compounding.

  • The v3.15.49 _target_grow_cycle_armed gate routes profit to
    realised_pnl WITHOUT growing target if the cycle is currently
    DISARMED. The cycle re-arms only when bb_pos reaches the
    opposing BB band. In a flat market that never reaches either
    extreme, this gate could explain "compounding feels insufficient"
    — but it's by design (prevents runaway one-direction growth).
    Operator did not request a change to this gate; flagged for
    awareness only.

WHAT WAS BUILT (v3.15.74):

  src/trading/smart_wire.py:
    • Lowered `min_wire_amount` default from $1.00 → $0.01.
    • distribute_fold_profit now emits visibility logs on every
      previously-silent path:
      - "WIRE FLOW (dust skip)" on both source and target buses when
        share < floor (lazy-imports get_event_bus to avoid coupling).
      - "WIRE FLOW (target unreachable)" on source bus when target
        bot ref is missing.
      - "WIRE FLOW (error)" on source bus when apply_wire_income
        raises.
      - "WIRE FLOW: fold $X produced no routed shares (...)" summary
        on source bus when EVERY route on a single fold failed.

  src/gui/main_window.py:
    • StatusLog._render dispatch broadened from
      `startswith("WIRE FLOW:")` (with colon) to
      `startswith("WIRE FLOW")` so the dust-skip / unreachable /
      error variants pick up the same magenta styling.
    • Also matches `startswith("WIRE INCOME")` so target-side income
      logs (distribute, pending, absorb) get matching magenta
      styling instead of plain text.

  tests/test_smart_wire_visibility.py (NEW, 9 cases):
    1. Default min_wire_amount is $0.01 (regression net).
    2. Explicit min_wire_amount override still honored.

    4. All-routes-filtered emits per-fold summary log.

SESSION: 2026-04-27 (Session 26 — continuation)
VERSIONS: v3.15.77
TITLE: Conditional opposing-direction hysteresis
================================================================================

OPERATOR DIRECTIVE (verbatim):
  "The opposing trade distance should not activate after one trade.
   The opposing directional movement should be confirmed first i.e.
   once the Target Delta begins drifting negative from the most
   recent Scrum. If the Target Delta goes positive again, it can
   deactivate. Similarly we need to have the opposing direction from
   a Fold to be the opposite with the Target Delta drifting positive
   to activate the gate. In markets that bouncing at the upper BB,
   this gate may flicker on and off frequently but that should be
   how it functions."

DIAGNOSIS (R68 cold-read of v3.15.52 hysteresis):

  v3.15.52 added an opposing-direction hysteresis: after a SCRUM,
  refuse the next FOLD until current price has fallen by interval+fee
  from the SCRUM price. After a FOLD, refuse the next SCRUM until
  price has risen by interval+fee from the FOLD price. The reference
  price was `_last_trade_price` — fixed across all subsequent ticks
  until the next fill.

  Operator's refinement: "armed-on-confirmation" model instead of
  "armed-immediately" model. The gate should:
    1. Stay disarmed after a fresh trade (delta near zero — opposing
       trade isn't going to fire from the main gate anyway).
    2. Arm when Target Delta CROSSES into opposing-direction territory
       (this is when the opposing trade becomes structurally possible).
    3. Capture the CURRENT price at arming as the new pivot reference
       (not the original trade price).
    4. Disarm when delta returns to same-as-last-trade direction.
    5. Re-arm with a fresh pivot when delta crosses opposing again.

  In a bouncing market each swing produces a fresh arm/disarm cycle —
  exactly the operator's "flicker on and off" intent.

WHAT WAS BUILT (v3.15.77):

  src/trading/scrumming_bot.py:

    Four new state fields in __init__:
      • _hyst_armed_fold_side: bool  (True when blocking FOLD)
      • _hyst_armed_scrum_side: bool (True when blocking SCRUM)
      • _hyst_ref_fold_side: float   (pivot price for FOLD-block)
      • _hyst_ref_scrum_side: float  (pivot price for SCRUM-block)

    New method _update_opposing_hysteresis_state(delta, price):
      • Called per-tick after delta is computed (before any gate
        consults the hysteresis).
      • If last trade was SCRUM:
        - delta < 0: arm FOLD-side at current price (if not already)
        - delta >= 0: disarm FOLD-side, clear ref
      • If last trade was FOLD: symmetric for SCRUM-side.
      • Emits operator-visible logs on each arm/disarm transition.

    New method _reset_opposing_hysteresis_after_fill():
      • Called from all 5 fill sites (regular SCRUM tick, regular
        FOLD tick, manual-fire SCRUM, manual-fire FOLD, self-destruct).
      • Resets both gates to disarmed/zero.
      • Next tick re-arms based on fresh delta direction.

    Updated gate sites:
      • _execute_sell SCRUM hysteresis block (~line 5573):
        condition `if (_hyst_armed_scrum_side and _hyst_ref_scrum_side > 0)`,
        reference `_hyst_ref_scrum_side` (was `_last_trade_price`).
      • _execute_buy FOLD hysteresis block (~line 5841):
        symmetric.
      • BB Priority Skew `_hyst_ok_*` in tick() (~line 3425):
        same change — uses armed state + pivot ref instead of
        last-trade-side + last-trade-price.

    Persistence:
      • export_scrumming_state writes 4 new fields, format_version
        bumped 3 → 4.
      • import_scrumming_state reads them with disarmed defaults
        (legacy v3 saves degrade cleanly).
      • Defensive self-heal: armed=True with ref=0 forced to
        disarmed on import.

THREE FIXES SHIPPED IN THIS CASCADE:

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FIX 1 — v3.15.78 — Pre-flight precision check
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  RCA: BotContainer.guarded_place_order placed orders with the
  exchange unconditionally. If the rounded-to-precision amount was
  below `min_amount`, the exchange rejected — but the API was hit
  every time. Operator's RAVE bot tried to SELL an amount that
  truncated below Coinbase's 0.1 precision floor; the exchange
  rejected; bot logged "SELL FAILED"; loop kept retrying.

  WHAT WAS BUILT:
    • New `_market_limits_cache` dict on BotContainer (per-bot,
      per-symbol). Lazy-loaded from exchange.get_markets().
    • New `_get_market_limits(symbol)` async helper. Returns
      (min_amount, min_cost, amount_precision); fail-open to
      (0,0,8) on any lookup error.
    • `guarded_place_order` performs pre-flight check BEFORE
      VolumeGuard or direct exchange.place_order:
        - Truncates (NOT rounds — banker's rounding bug; 0.05
          → 0.1 with round-half-to-even) amount to precision.
        - If truncated < min_amount: raise PRE-FLIGHT REJECTED.
        - If amount × price < min_cost: raise PRE-FLIGHT REJECTED.
      Existing call sites' SELL FAILED: {exc} / BUY FAILED: {exc}
      logging surface the marker cleanly.

  TESTS: tests/test_preflight_precision_check.py (13 cases all
  green): cache init/lookup/cache/fail-open, dust skip + below-
  min/cost paths emit + don't hit API, above-min passes through,
  market-order with no price skips cost check, error message
  includes diagnostics, static-text pin.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FIX 2 — v3.15.78 — LogManager bus attachment
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  RCA: LogManager defined log_trade(), log_ta_signal(), log_pnl()
  and constructed an NDJSONWriter for logs/real_market/trade.log
  in __init__ — but no caller invoked log_trade. The writer was
  built but never written to. Trades emitted on the in-process
  event bus as "trade.filled"; the GUI consumed them; the on-disk
  persistence path was orphaned. Operator's logs/real_market/
  contained only system.log and pnl/ — never trade.log.

  WHAT WAS BUILT:
    • New `LogManager.attach_to_bus(bus)` subscribes a handler
      for trade.filled events. Idempotent (re-subscribing
      replaces).
    • New `LogManager._on_trade_filled_bus(event)` normalizes
      both event shapes (kwargs and data={...}) and calls
      log_trade(). Fail-soft: any exception logged at warning
      and swallowed.
    • main.py now calls log_manager.attach_to_bus(bus)
      immediately after constructing both.

  TESTS: tests/test_log_manager_bus_attach.py (8 cases all
  green): construction silent, kwargs-style event lands in NDJSON,
  data={...}-style normalizes, multiple trades append (no
  overwrite), idempotent re-attach doesn't double-write,
  malformed event fails-soft, main.py wires after bus, methods
  present.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FIX 3 — v3.15.79 — Cartridge gate respects hysteresis
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Operator-reported timeline:
    16:35:59  Bot FOLDED 0.02138672 ETH @ $2295.13 = $49.48
    16:37:00  MAX CARTRIDGE FIRE (SCRUM): |delta|=$47.78 ≥ $5.14
    16:37:01  Cartridge SCRUM 0.02081043 ETH @ $2295.89 = $47.40
    Net: round-trip loss after fees on a 0.03% price move.

  RCA: v3.15.63 cartridge gate explicitly bypassed v3.15.77
  opposing-direction hysteresis (the very gate the operator
  designed to prevent fee-thrash round-trips). Bypass justified
  at v3.15.63 ship as "manual-fire path bypasses everything because
  operator is sovereign", but cartridge is automatic, not
  operator-initiated, so the bypass produced money loss.

  TICK-ORDER AMPLIFIER: v3.15.77 hysteresis update lived at
  line ~3276, AFTER the cartridge gate at ~2925. So immediately
  after a fill (_reset_opposing_hysteresis_after_fill cleared
  armed=False), the NEXT tick's cartridge gate saw stale
  armed=False and fired BEFORE the same tick's hysteresis
  update could re-arm. Operator's bot misfired exactly here.

  WHAT WAS BUILT:
    1. Tick-order corrected — hysteresis update moved to
       immediately after current_value computation (line ~2790).
       Cartridge gate at ~2925 now sees fresh state.
    2. Cartridge gate now consults v3.15.77 hysteresis state:
         • SCRUM proposed + _hyst_armed_scrum_side + price <
           pivot × (1 + interval+fee) ⇒ refuse.
         • FOLD proposed + _hyst_armed_fold_side + price >
           pivot × (1 - interval+fee) ⇒ refuse.
       On refusal: throttled "MAX CARTRIDGE BLOCKED" log; do
       NOT return (let normal SCRUM/FOLD continue, which also
       respect hysteresis).
    3. Gate NOT disabled. Operator was explicit: "DO NOT
       DISABLE THE FUCKING GATE — FIX IT." When delta runs
       away AND hysteresis is clear, cartridge still fires.
    4. Cartridge still bypasses (intentional): BB Detection,
       soft CB, higher-TF bias. Those are entry/regime gates,
       not anti-thrash gates.

  TESTS: tests/test_cartridge_respects_hysteresis.py (6 cases
  all green):
    1. Operator's exact ETH scenario blocks cartridge
    2. Runaway delta with clear hysteresis still fires
    3. Tick-order: update precedes cartridge gate
    4. Gate references all four hysteresis fields
    5. Gate is ENABLED (no kill-switch / hard-disable)
    6. Post-fill reset → next-tick arming → cartridge blocks
       (the FULL chain that produced the operator's incident)

  Existing test_max_cartridge_size.py updated to widen static-
  text search windows (v3.15.79 comment block pushed fire path
  ~10k chars further down the file).

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

SESSION KEY INSIGHT (R68 reflection):

  This session's recurring failure mode is "bypass without audit."
  Five operator-reported issues, all stem from the same pattern:
  some part of the codebase has a SAFETY gate (hysteresis, dust
  filter, threshold, write path), and another part of the codebase
  bypasses it — explicitly OR by accident — without proving the
  bypass is safe in EVERY caller.

    v3.15.74 — Smart Wire dust silently dropped (no log on skip)
    v3.15.75 — MEM-196 constants ignored operator thresholds
    v3.15.77 — Hysteresis used fixed reference instead of swing pivot
    v3.15.78 — LogManager.log_trade defined but never called +
               guarded_place_order didn't pre-flight precision
    v3.15.79 — Cartridge bypassed v3.15.77 hysteresis

  Going forward: any code path that says "bypasses everything"
  must be CALLER-AUDITED. "Operator-initiated manual fire bypasses"
  is correct (operator is sovereign). "Automated path that reuses
  the manual-fire machinery" inherits that bypass without the
  operator-sovereign justification — and produces money loss.

SESSION: 2026-04-27 (Session 26 — continuation)
VERSIONS: v3.15.80
TITLE: Multi-base isolation refreshed per-tick
================================================================================

OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-04-27:
  "ETH:USDC bot appears to have frozen after the ETH:USDT bot sold
   some ETH. They appear to be sharing the same Target Delta
   calculation rather than having any Base Currency protection that
   would prevent conflicts. Just verified that both ETH bots are
   locked to the same Target Delta feed. Need to isolate and
   prevent errors."

ROOT CAUSE: v3.15.56 multi-base attribution flag set ONCE at init.
  ETH/USDC bot inits alone → flag=False → reads shared exchange
  pool. ETH/USDT created later → its flag=True correctly. ETH/USDC's
  flag never re-evaluated → keeps reading shared pool → ETH/USDT
  trades drop the pool → ETH/USDC sees phantom deficit → freezes
  on safety guards.

FIX (v3.15.80): _refresh_multi_base_isolation(current_price) runs
  per-tick before current_value computation. On False→True
  transition with non-zero holdings + empty _main_lots, seeds a
  single lot capturing current holdings at current price (best-
  effort cost basis). Without the seed, transitioned bot would
  see zero attributed units and freeze.

TESTS: tests/test_multi_base_isolation_per_tick.py (8 cases,
all green): seed-on-transition, no-duplicate-lots, zero-holdings-
no-seed, sibling-departs-preserves-lots, idempotent, no-manager-
fail-soft, tick-order pin, signature pin. Consolidated battery:
344/344 green.

PATTERN NOTE (sixth occurrence this session): set-once init state
where the underlying condition is runtime-mutable. The lesson —
"runtime-mutable state needs runtime-mutable checks" — applies to
every gate / guard / flag the operator can change post-init.

## Session 27 — v3.18.5 — Crash mitigation: GC centralization (2026-05-19)

Operator-observed platform crash 2026-05-19 ~08:53 running v3.18.1. Diagnosed from `~/.acervator_logs/faulthandler_20260519_085308.log` + watchdog postmortem as Windows STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION on a CCXT worker thread mid-JSON-parse, triggered by CPython's automatic GC firing while urllib3/OpenSSL C-extension state was held. Main thread was incidentally in indicator_panel.paintEvent at the same instant.

Three application-level fixes shipped:

1. **GC centralization** — disable automatic GC, run gc.collect() on a QTimer (5s cadence) from the GUI thread. Concentrates GC pauses on a known-safe thread, eliminates the worker-thread GC race surface.

2. **Logger silencing + watchdog rotation** — ccxt and urllib3 loggers dropped to WARNING (the v3.18.1 postmortem bundle contained a 6.7 GB console log from per-request DEBUG-level HTTP-header dumps). ChildRunner in acervator_watchdog.py adds 100 MB size-based rotation with 3 backups as defense in depth.

3. **CCXT pool audit** — confirmed MEM-220 already caps each connector at max_workers=1. The 20+ ccxt-coinbase_0 threads in the faulthandler are from 20+ per-bot connector instances (one per active bot), which is architecturally expected. No additional pool changes needed.

Operator explicitly rejected the alternative path of downgrading Python ("does not consider what the update fixed"). Application-level fix preserves the 3.14 upgrade benefits while eliminating the same race window.

MEM-263. Ship gate: syntax clean, version sync, 1334 pass / 24 fail / 0 crash (no new regressions from this ship).

## Session 27 — v3.18.15 — P1 Manual Fire audit: operator-sovereignty invariant restored (2026-05-20)

Operator directive: "Proceed. We are doing great." Selected P1 Manual Fire audit from the queued items.

The R68 self-audit caught a real mistake in the prior ship. v3.18.14 placed the MEM-257 helper call inside the shared _execute_manual_rebalance method. That method has three callers: Manual Fire (operator-initiated, scrumming_bot.py:3876), Wire Stack (auto, 3918), Max Cartridge (auto, 4162). The v3.18.14 placement intercepted all three — including the operator-initiated Manual Fire path. The Session 26 close invariant says "Manual Fire is the operator-authorized override. It MUST bypass every gate." v3.18.14 violated that invariant.

Empirical verification with tests/test_bonk_restart_phantom_buy.py scaffolding: setting _manual_fire_pending=True in a BONK phantom-zero scenario triggered the MEM-257 refusal — operator's click was being blocked.

Operator chose the "Move MEM-257 to auto-fire call sites only" path. Strict operator-sovereignty.

Architectural fix: three edits to scrumming_bot.py. (1) Removed the v3.18.14 _verify_buy_safe_or_refuse insertion from inside _execute_manual_rebalance. (2) Inserted the helper-call at the Max Cartridge call site (~line 4154), gated on _direction == "FOLD" (BUY-side only). (3) Inserted the helper-call at the Wire Stack call site (~line 3917, always a buy). Manual Fire path (line 3876) deliberately untouched.

Why this separation matters: auto-fire paths are the bot deciding on its own that conditions warrant a buy — MEM-257 catches "state is lying". Manual Fire is the operator bringing independent verification the bot doesn't have. Putting MEM-257 on this path conflates "bot is confused" with "operator wants to override the bot's confusion."

Tests: one new pinning test — test_manual_fire_bypasses_mem257_per_operator_invariant (Test 6). Same BONK phantom-zero setup as Test 5 but sets _manual_fire_pending=True. Asserts place_order proceeds + no MEM-257 refusal log. Future regression detector for the operator-sovereignty invariant. Test 5 (Max Cartridge defense pin from MEM-272) still passes — helper is at call site instead of inside method, semantic preserved.

Test suite: 1399/0/0 (was 1398/0/0; +1 from new Test 6; zero regressions).

The R68 self-audit caught its own author's mistake before the operator did — exactly what R68 is supposed to enable.

----- v3.19.5 root-cause closure (same ship) -----
Operator reported 2026-05-20: the mid-cascade host crash root cause was ~/.acervator_logs/ accumulating to ~400 GB and crashing the host. v3.18.5 had capped per-RUN log file rotation (ROTATE_BYTES=100MB × ROTATE_KEEP=3 = 400 MB max per run) but never capped the NUMBER of accumulated postmortem_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS/ directories — each crash/restart cycle wrote a fresh bundle copying the console log + crash log + faulthandler log + py-spy dump (easily 100s of MB per bundle), and over weeks of restarts these grew unbounded.

Fix in acervator_watchdog.py: prune_postmortem_bundles(keep_latest=20, max_age_days=30) retention policy + report_log_dir_footprint() with 5 GB WARNING threshold at watchdog startup so any future runaway is operator-visible BEFORE it crashes the host. Wired at two sites: _run_watchdog() on startup (closes accumulated bloat from prior runs) AND after each write_postmortem() bundle (caps mid-session accumulation if a single run produces many crash/restart cycles).

tests/test_postmortem_rotation.py — 13 contract pins covering count cap, age cap, no-op-on-fresh-dir, missing-log-dir safety, non-postmortem-sibling-untouched safety, survives-undeletable-bundle resilience (Windows file-lock case), return-tuple shape, footprint reporter paths, dir-size helper, plus TWO source-introspection wiring drift detectors that ast-walk _run_watchdog and write_postmortem to assert each contains a Call to prune_postmortem_bundles. If a future refactor removes either call, the test breaks loudly.

Final suite: 1518/0/0 (was 1488/0/0; +17 v3.19.5 sim tests; +13 postmortem-rotation tests; +32 cp1252 environmental failures closed in-ship).

The baselines prevent silent backsliding while the backfill work proceeds in future ships.

LIMITATIONS HONESTLY DOCUMENTED:

Defensive on missing bb_proximity (returns triggered=False) and missing bollinger_bands signal (bb_position sentinel -1.0). detect_w_bottom(candles, bb_pos_history, lower_threshold=0.10, midline_recovery=0.40, min_separation=5, lookback=30) implements canonical Bollinger W-Bottom: two lower-band tests with second at HIGHER price AND HIGHER bb_pos, midline recovery in between. Returns rich diagnostic dict with both test indices, prices, bb_pos values, and pullback details. detect_m_top is the mirror (upper_threshold=0.90, midline_pullback=0.60, second high LOWER + lower bb_pos).

Architectural contract: all three return dict (not Signal) — explicit 'structural detector' shape distinct from voting indicators. The dict-return makes future Tier-1 composites trivially additive without conflating with VotingEngine signal aggregation.

Tests: tests/test_l1_l2_structural_detectors.py with 18 contract pins. Spring (8): canonical trigger; each-component-missing variant; defensive missing-bb-proximity; defensive missing-bb-signal; configurable threshold. W-Bottom (5): canonical pattern triggers with diagnostics; rejects second-test-lower (breakdown); requires midline_recovery; misaligned bb_history defensive; no-pattern diagnostic. M-Top (3): canonical bearish pattern triggers; rejects second-test-higher (breakout); cross-check on W-Bottom data. Cross-check (1): W-Bottom doesn't fire on M-Top data. Architectural contract (1): all detectors return dict with triggered bool + name string — catches regression to bare bool or Signal return.

Fix: target_asset = `*` (pool sigil) so BotConfig.__post_init__ constructs symbol = `*/{base}` — clear multi-pair indicator visible in titles, audit logs, and downstream displays.

Bug 1: CRYPTO_CORRELATIONS had 8 of 15 keys in wrong order making most correlations unreachable. get_correlation does tuple(sorted([a, b])) before lookup but table stored keys in arbitrary order (e.g. ('BTC', 'AVAX'): 0.75 - sorted lookup produces ('AVAX', 'BTC') which misses). Affected pairs BTC/AVAX BTC/ADA ETH/AVAX ETH/DOT ETH/ADA SOL/AVAX SOL/DOT LINK/DOT - most non-BTC/ETH cross-correlations silently defaulting to 0.3. Risk manager correlated_exposure rule was under-firing as a result. Fix: keys re-stored in sorted-tuple form + test_correlation_table_keys_are_sorted_tuples structural invariant prevents recurrence. Bug 2: RiskManager instances shared mutable RiskRule state via DEFAULT_RULES class attribute. __init__ dict comprehension stored references to shared class-level dataclass instances so when one RiskManager triggered max_drawdown and set last_triggered=now every subsequent RiskManager() started with already-set cooldown - rule effectively un-triggerable for rest of session. Also affected threshold/enabled overrides via set_rule. Fix: dataclasses.replace() in __init__ gives each instance its own RiskRule copies. Existing v3.19.22 test_risk_manager_instantiates_with_all_default_rules updated from identity 'is' assertion to field-equality + explicit NOT-IS (the v3.19.39 decoupling intentionally breaks identity to enforce instance-state isolation).

Discovery pattern: test failures in BATCH but passing ALONE was the smoking gun for shared mutable state. The CRYPTO_CORRELATIONS bug surfaced via explicit test_correlation_table_keys_are_sorted_tuples structural invariant.

==================== v3.20.7 — 2026-05-23 ====================
ZScoreExtremityGate (gate #17) ships, closing v3.20.6 audit Finding #5 and the v3.19.17 forward-work item. Asymmetric SCRUM/FOLD design: side="scrum" blocks SCRUM when z < -2.0 (don't sell the statistical bottom); side="fold" blocks FOLD when z > +2.0 (don't buy the statistical top). Asymmetry intentional -- each side filters only its contrarian-wrong action, never the contrarian-right one. Sentinel discipline: 0.0 doubles as "not populated" + "at mean", in either case |z|=0 < threshold so gate passes naturally without a special branch. ## Session 27 - v3.20.41 - Patent filing-status language correction (2026-06-01)

Operator correction 2026-06-01: 'Nothing has been filed and I never claimed this...' flagging the Part 2 Filing Status callout which had stated "Priority dates are established by the dated MEM entries in the repository's EPISODIC_MEMORY.json, timestamped at commit time, and are available for attorney review. Recommended filing order tracks this catalogue." This was a legal-claim overreach that I should never have written. MEM entries with commit timestamps do NOT establish patent priority dates in any legal sense; only a filed patent application does. No attorney has been engaged; no application has been filed; no filing strategy has been determined. The operator never made any of these claims. CHANGES: (1) Part 2 Filing Status callout rewritten with honest framing including explicit statements that none of the 26 inventions have been filed, none are 'patent-pending' in the legal sense, the MEM entries are internal documentation with no legal standing as priority dates, only a filed application establishes priority, no attorney has been engaged, and no filing strategy has been determined. (2) Part 1 Copyright NOTICE paragraph corrected from "patented, patent-pending, or intended for patent filing" to "claimed as novel and intends as candidates for future patent filing. No applications have been filed as of publication; nothing in this document is 'patent-pending' in the legal sense." The license-prohibition clause is retained. (3) Other patent-language sites audited and confirmed acceptable: Part 1 PATENT NOTICE CalloutBox already uses correct conditional framing ("may constitute patent infringement once claims are granted") and is unchanged. Part 2 entry-structure "(6) Claim Scope - draft patent-claim language ready for attorney review" describes the format of catalogued entries, not an actual attorney engagement, and is unchanged. ROOT-CAUSE LESSON: legal claims about IP status require careful language discipline - "priority dates established by" and "patent-pending" are specific legal designations that require formal filings.
